author: toshiotawa
body: Fixes note and audio synchronization in Fantasy Mode by correcting `getCurrentMusicTime()` calculation and adding debug logs for verification. The previous `getCurrentMusicTime()` implementation in `BGMManager.ts` incorrectly calculated the music time, especially when pitch shifting was active (using Tone.js) or during the count-in period. The modulo operator (`%`) was misapplied, causing the time to reset within the loop duration even during the initial count-in phase, leading to notes appearing at the wrong times relative to the audio. This PR ensures that `getCurrentMusicTime()` returns negative values for the count-in period and 0 for M1 Beat 1, providing a consistent time reference for note rendering across all playback methods. ---

author: methodmanav
body:
## Proposed Changes

- Fixes #1819 

## Problem

First-time developers copying `.env.example` to `.env.local` encounter Zod validation errors 

This occurs because some environment variables are marked as **optional** while still using `.min(1)`:

- `.optional()` allows the value to be `undefined`
- `.min(1)` explicitly disallows empty strings (`""`)

When a variable exists in `.env` but is left empty (`VAR=`), it is parsed as an empty string rather than `undefined`. As a result, validation fails even though the variable is intended to be optional.

Since optional environment variables in `.env.example` are commonly left empty, this breaks local setup for new contributors.

---

## Solution

Empty strings are transformed to `undefined` for optional environment variables before validation, preserving strict validation for non-empty values.

### Before
```ts
INTERNAL_SLACK_USER_ID: z.string().min(1).optional(),
SLACK_OAUTH_TOKEN: z.string().min(1).optional(),

### After
```ts
INTERNAL_SLACK_USER_ID: z.string().transform(allowEmptyString).optional(),
SLACK_OAUTH_TOKEN: z.string().transform(allowEmptyString).optional(),

body: Add schema-aware chat message fetching and a migration to fix the `message_type` column missing error and improve chat robustness. The original error `column chat_messages.message_type does not exist` caused chat message fetching to fail entirely. This PR introduces a new `_fetch_chat_messages` utility that dynamically adjusts the `SELECT` query to exclude missing columns, preventing hard failures. It also normalizes message data, ensuring `message_type` defaults to 'text' and other fields like `media_url` and `metadata` are present. A SQL migration is included to add and backfill the `message_type` column, and new message inserts now include `content` and `message` fields for backward compatibility with older schema versions. ---

author: sungwoob
body:
### Motivation
- Allow dataset paths for `data`, `x`, `y`, `genotype_dir`, and `phenotype_dir` to be provided in the YAML config so the script does not require CLI-only input for those paths.
- Let CLI flags continue to override config values so users can prefer either method interchangeably.
- Reuse the resolved dataset paths with the existing multi-target AutoML flow to keep behavior consistent when running multiple targets.

### Description
- Added `resolve_data_paths(config, args)` which reads paths from the config and uses CLI `args` values as overrides and returns a dict with `data_path`, `x_path`, `y_path`, `genotype_dir`, and `phenotype_dir`.
- Updated `main()` to call `resolve_data_paths()` and pass resolved paths into `load_dataset()` instead of reading `args` directly.
- Adjusted `load_dataset()` signature to accept `genotype_dir`, `phenotype_dir`, and `target_columns` and added validation for required `target_column(s)` when using `data_path` or genotype/phenotype inputs, and single-target enforcement for `y_path` input.
- Updated `config.yaml` to document new keys (`data_path`, `x_path`, `y_path`, `genotype_dir`, `phenotype_dir`) and retained support for `target_columns` as a list.

author: saulshanabrook
body:
This PR adds support for running the tests locally to produce code coverage and in CI uploading to Codecov.

This should allow us to see for each PR how it affects the overall code coverage and what added lines are covered by tests/examples. I have been finding myself wanting this, as I develop new features to make sure I covered all the cases with examples.

I don't suggest we require 100% coverage for new lines added. However, even just seeing the lines can help you understand if your tests are covering what you think they are and possibly encourage covering more lines.

It can also help see what parts of our code base are not used in any examples.

author: mahdirasoulian
body:
### Motivation
- Fix MT5 `order_send` failures caused by the Python wrapper rejecting requests with non-native types (error `(-2, "Unnamed arguments not allowed")`).
- Make request construction consistent across MARKET/LIMIT/STOP to prevent bad keys/field mismatches when switching order types (e.g., RiskManager switching STOP→MARKET).
- Add observability to capture the exact types sent to `mt5.order_send` for faster diagnosis if wrapper marshaling fails again.

### Description
- Add `sanitize_mt5_request(request: dict)` and `_to_native_value` to coerce `numpy`, `pandas`, `Decimal` and similar scalars into native Python types and to drop `None` values before calling `mt5.order_send`.
- Centralize order construction in `build_order_request(...)` which validates required fields and maps action/type names to MT5 constants for MARKET/LIMIT/STOP requests.
- Update `_order_send_with_retry` to call `sanitize_mt5_request`, log `REQ_TYPES` and `REQ_DATA` immediately before `mt5.order_send`, and retry with the sanitized dict on reconnect.
- Replace ad-hoc request dict creation in market/limit/stop send paths to use `build_order_request`, and add `scripts/mt5_order_send_repro.py` to reproduce and print sanitized requests and field types (supports `--dry-run`).

### Testing
- No automated tests were run on this patch.

author: rafaelmeloreisnovo
body:
### Motivation
- Improve runtime resilience and observability by capturing uncaught exceptions and classifying common network failures for friendlier domain errors.
- Harden startup locale and preferences access to avoid race conditions and reduce unnecessary Compose recompositions.
- Provide offline-first fallbacks for GitHub lookups and validate clone targets to fail early on permission issues.

### Description
- Added a global uncaught exception handler and wired structured logging via `ErrorHandler.initialize` and `GlobalExceptionHandler`, and created a coroutine exception handler for the application scope in `RafGitToolsApplication` to log uncaught/coroutine exceptions.
- Implemented trust-on-first-use (TOFU) signature verification backed by `DataStore` in `SecurityManager` with `verifyTrustedSignature`, and clarified method documentation to reflect TOFU behavior.
- Mapped cleartext/HTTP-related `IOException` to a new domain error `AppError.NetworkError.CleartextNotPermitted` and updated `ErrorType.fromException` and `Throwable.toAppError()` to detect cleartext messages.
- Added offline-first cache helpers in `AsyncCacheManager` and `RepositoryNameCacheDao`, and updated `GithubDataRepository` to return cached `RepositoryNameCache` / `UserCache` results when network calls fail using `toAppError()` normalization.
- Added `validateCloneTarget` in `JGitService` to check filesystem permissions and create parent directories early, and enabled actual branch deletion flow in `BranchListViewModel` to call `gitRepository.deleteBranch` with success/error handling.
- Made preferences and localization safer by introducing a `Mutex` in `PreferencesRepository` and `LocalizationManager` and added `applyLocale` to avoid race conditions; reduced Compose recompositions in `LanguageSelector` with `remember` and stable keys.
- Removed placeholder certificate pinning blocks from `network_security_config.xml` and filled other placeholders across the codebase.

### Testing
- Updated unit test `app/src/test/kotlin/com/rafgittools/domain/error/AppErrorTest.kt` to verify that a cleartext `IOException` maps to `AppError.NetworkError.CleartextNotPermitted` and that `UnknownHostException` maps to `AppError.NetworkError.NoConnection` (tests added/modified).
- No automated test run was executed as part of this change; unit tests were introduced/updated but not run in CI during this changeset.

body:
### Motivation

- Convert the old tags UI to a 2-mode “Browse/Assign → Edit” flow so the tag editor controls are hidden by default and surface only when creating or editing a tag.
- Make creating/attaching tags explicit and discoverable with an always-visible Add bar and Return-to-add behavior.
- Add ad-hoc custom hex colors per-tag with a Random Hex control and ensure tag chips remain single-line and visually consistent.

### Description

- Reworked the tags UI in `ScaleLibrarySheet.swift` by replacing the old inline editor with a browse view and a bottom editor drawer implemented as `TagsBrowseView` and `TagEditorDrawer` overlay, using `.overlay(alignment:.bottom)` plus `.transition(.move(edge:.bottom).combined(with:.opacity))` and a spring animation.
- Implemented Add bar and search flow in the browse view so typing + Return or tapping `Add` will attach an existing tag or create-and-attach a new tag and auto-open the editor drawer when creating a new tag.
- Implemented long-press/context-menu Edit… on tag chips in both assigned and all-tags lists to present the editor drawer (rename/icon/color controls live-update global TagStore state).
- Added Random Hex support and per-tag custom hex persistence: `TagRef.customHex`, helpers `resolvedColor`/`resolvedHex`, and `TagColor.hexValue` mapping in `TagModels.swift` to resolve a displayed color/hex.
- Extended `TagStore` to persist `customHex` and added `setTagCustomHex(id:hex:)`; `setTagColor` now clears any `customHex` so palette selection wins as before.
- Updated `TagPickerUI.swift` `TagChip` to enforce one-line labels with `.lineLimit(1)` and `.truncationMode(.tail)` and to use the resolved color for chip fill/outline so Random Hex immediately updates chip appearance.
- Editor drawer includes icon picker, color palette, a Random Hex button (generates `#%06X`, applies immediately, triggers a light haptic on iOS, and the hex text is tappable to copy), and a name field that commits normalized renames and handles merging.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed for this change in this environment; please run your Xcode unit/UI tests or CI to validate build and behavior.

### [`v0.98.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/releases/tag/v0.98.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/compare/v0.97.2...v0.98.0)

#### ✨ New Features

##### The `--filter` flag now implies `--all`

When using the `--filter` flag, it is now optional to also supply `--all`. Terragrunt will automatically set the `--all` flag when you use the `--filter` flag.

#### 🐛 Bug Fixes

##### Plan files are now correctly passed as CLI arguments for destroy operations

A bug in the logic used for injecting plan files as arguments to the `apply -destroy` command resulted in the plan file argument being injected prior to the `-auto-approve` flag, which is disallowed in OpenTofu/Terraform. That bug has been fixed.

##### GCS bootstrap authentication fixed

A bug in the authentication logic for GCS backends prevented successful bootstrapping of backends when using the `--auth-provider-cmd` flag. That bug has been fixed.

##### Git-based and Graph-based combinations fixed

A bug in the discovery logic for Git worktrees prevented using a combination of Git-based and Graph-based filter expressions in the same filter from working correctly.

e.g.

```bash
 terragrunt find --filter '...^[HEAD^...HEAD]...'
```

That bug has been fixed.

##### Proper exit codes returned from `-detailed-exitcode`

A bug in the logic for handling retries combined with the OpenTofu/Terraform `plan -detailed-exitcode` and the Terragrunt `--all` flag resulted in the wrong exit code being returned when a failed run succeeded on a subsequent retry with a status code related to drift (exit code 2).

That logic has been corrected, and properly follows the rules outlined under the [`--all`](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/docs/reference/cli/commands/run/#all) flag:

When not using `-detailed-exitcode`:

- Terragrunt will return the highest exit code of all runs performed.

When using `-detailed-exitcode`:

- If any run has an exit code that is 1, or greater than 2, `run --all` will return the highest exit code.
- Otherwise, if any run returns an exit code of 2, `run --all` will return an exit code of 2.
- Otherwise, `run --all` will return an exit code of 0.

##### OpenTelemetry traces in console mode fixed

A bug in OpenTelemetry trace exporting prevented traces from being exported when in console mode. That bug has been fixed.

##### Negation logic fixed

A bug in how negation logic was handled in filter expressions prevented successful exclusion of stacks from generation and over excluded units in runs when users only supplied negative filters.

#### ⚙️ Process Improvements

##### GPG Signing

Release artifacts are now signed using both GPG and Cosign.

To start performing signature validation on assets, in addition to the asset you’re downloading from the GitHub releases page, you’ll want to download some of the following files:

The workflow was not triggering for PRs submitted from branches within the same repository due to an overly restrictive `if` condition that required PRs to originate from forks.

## Changes

- **Removed fork-only restriction** from the `process-pr` job condition
- Workflow now triggers for any PR with 'submit' in the title, regardless of source repository

## Before/After

**Before:**
```yaml
if: >-
  github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository &&
  contains(lower(github.event.pull_request.title), 'submit')
```

**After:**
```yaml
if: contains(lower(github.event.pull_request.title), 'submit')
```

The existing fork/same-repo detection logic (lines 47-57) remains unchanged and correctly handles both scenarios.

## Summary
- Completed Microservice Initialization section
- Added BullMQ queue system with Redis
- Created Strapi API client for all content types

## Changes

### Queue System (BullMQ + Redis)
- Redis connection with retry logic and health monitoring
- Review queue with 3 concurrent workers and rate limiting (10 jobs/min)
- Exponential backoff for failed jobs (3 attempts)

Fixes two critical error logging bugs in CRD application:

body:
The `/ytdlp` command only accepted URLs with hardcoded parameters (format sorting, mp4 recoding, filename restrictions), preventing users from customizing downloads via yt-dlp flags.

## Changes

**Command parsing**
- Parse flags (prefixed with `-`/`--`) separately from URLs
- Detect URLs by `://` presence to avoid consuming them as flag values
- Pass both flags and URLs to task execution

**Task execution**
- Accept custom flags array in `ytdlp.Task`
- Pass flags to yt-dlp before URLs: `[FLAGS...] [URLS...]`
- Apply default behavior (format sorting, recoding) only when no flags provided
- Always preserve output path for temp directory safety

**Data flow**
- Added `YtdlpFlags []string` to `tcbdata.Add` and `ytdlp.Task`
- Updated handler chain: `handleYtdlpCmd` → `CreateAndAddYtdlpTaskWithEdit` → `NewTask`

**i18n**
- Updated usage messages with flag examples (EN/CN)

## Usage

```bash
# Backward compatible
/ytdlp https://example.com/video

# With custom flags
/ytdlp --format best https://example.com/video
/ytdlp --extract-audio --audio-format mp3 https://example.com/video

# Multiple URLs
/ytdlp --format best https://example.com/v1 https://example.com/v2
```

Flags and URLs can be mixed in any order. The parser correctly differentiates between flag values and URLs.

author: copilot
body:
Production-ready system tray application for managing OpenVPN connections on Arch Linux / KDE Plasma (X11). Uses `ksni` for native StatusNotifierItem support with intent-aware auto-reconnect to prevent zombie reconnection loops.

## Implementation

- **VpnActor (async actor pattern)**: Process supervision runs separately from GUI thread to keep UI responsive during reconnection attempts
- **Intent tracking**: Distinguishes user-initiated disconnects from unexpected drops—auto-reconnect only triggers on unintentional disconnection
- **State machine**: `Disconnected` → `Connecting` → `Connected` ↔ `Retrying` with dynamic icon colors (red/yellow/green)
- **Auto-reconnect**: 5-second delay, max 5 attempts, toggleable via menu checkbox
- **Server switching**: Cleanly terminates current connection before establishing new one

## Connection flow

```rust
// Connect via pkexec for privilege escalation
Command::new("pkexec")
    .arg("openvpn")
    .arg("--config").arg(&config_path)
    .arg("--auth-user-pass").arg(AUTH_FILE)
    .spawn()

// Graceful disconnect via SIGTERM
signal::kill(Pid::from_raw(pid as i32), Signal::SIGTERM)
```

## Dependencies

- `ksni` - Native KDE SNI support (not tray-icon/libappindicator)
- `tokio` - Async runtime with process/signal features
- `notify-rust` - Desktop notifications
- `nix` - Signal handling

> Finalized AI Prompt (with Auto-Reconnect)
> Role: Act as a Senior Rust Systems Programmer specialized in Linux Desktop environments (Arch/KDE).
> 
> Task: Build a production-ready system tray application for managing OpenVPN connections with auto-reconnect capabilities.
> 
> Target Environment:
> 
> OS: Arch Linux
> Desktop: KDE Plasma (X11)
> Tray Standard: StatusNotifierItem (SNI) via DBus
> Technical Stack (Strict Requirements):
> 
> Language: Rust (1.92.0 or newer).
> Tray Crate: ksni (Do NOT use tray-icon or libappindicator; ksni is native for KDE).
> Async Runtime: tokio with process, fs, time, and signal features.
> Privilege Escalation: pkexec (Polkit) for the OpenVPN binary execution.
> Notifications: notify-rust (using D-Bus).
> Functional Requirements:
> 
> State Management & Auto-Reconnect:
> Maintain distinct states: Disconnected, Connecting, Connected(ServerName), and Retrying.
> Intentional vs. Accidental: You must track intent. If the user clicks "Disconnect", auto-reconnect is disabled. If the process exits unexpectedly (non-zero code or signal) while the state was Connected, trigger the auto-reconnect logic.
> Retry Logic: If connection drops, wait 5 seconds and retry indefinitely (or up to 5 times) until successful. Update the icon to yellow/orange during retries.
> Tray Menu & Icon:
> Icon: Dynamic icons (Green=Connected, Yellow=Connecting/Retrying, Red=Disconnected).
> Menu: Dynamically populate a list of .ovpn files from /etc/openvpn/.
> Controls: "Auto-Reconnect" toggle in the menu (checkbox style).
> Connection Logic:
> Connect: pkexec openvpn --config /etc/openvpn/<file> --auth-user-pass /etc/openvpn/auth.txt
> Disconnect: Send SIGTERM to the specific child process ID.
> Switching: If user clicks Server B while connected to Server A: Disconnect A -> Wait for exit -> Connect B.
> Parsing:
> Clean filenames for the menu (e.g., us8399.nordvpn.com.udp.ovpn -> us8399).
> Deliverables:
> 
> Cargo.toml: Include ksni, tokio, notify-rust, regex, and libc.
> main.rs: Modular code. Implement a VpnActor struct that handles the process supervision loop separately from the GUI thread to ensure the UI never freezes during reconnection attempts.
> Arch Setup Instructions: A brief comment listing necessary pacman packages.
> Key changes for the AI:
> Intent Tracking: I explicitly asked the AI to track intent. Without this, your app would get stuck in a "zombie loop" where you click Disconnect, and it immediately tries to reconnect you because it thinks the VPN crashed.
> UI Toggle: Added a checkbox in the menu so you can easily turn this feature off if you're on a bad network.
> VpnActor: Requested an actor pattern. This is crucial for Rust async apps; otherwise, your tray icon will become unresponsive while the app sleeps for 5 seconds waiting to reconnect.


</details>

body:
## Summary

Created `CommandsApiController` with 3 AJAX endpoints for seamless tab switching on the Commands page:

**Endpoints:**
1. **GET /api/commands/list** - Returns command list partial view (_CommandListTab.cshtml)
   - Displays all registered slash commands with modules, parameters, and preconditions
   - Uses ICommandMetadataService.GetAllModulesAsync()

2. **GET /api/commands/logs** - Returns filtered/paginated execution logs (_ExecutionLogsTab.cshtml)
   - Query params: startDate, endDate, guildId, searchTerm, commandName, statusFilter, pageNumber, pageSize
   - Parameter validation: max pageSize 100, min pageNumber 1, max 90-day date range
   - Desktop table view and mobile card view with pagination

3. **GET /api/commands/analytics** - Returns analytics with Chart.js visualizations (_AnalyticsTab.cshtml)
   - Query params: startDate (default 30 days ago), endDate (default today), guildId
   - Date range validation: max 90 days
   - Metrics cards and 4 charts (commands by module, execution trends, success rate, top commands)

**Key Features:**
- Server-side rendered HTML partial views (SSR for all endpoints)
- RequireModerator authorization at controller level
- Comprehensive error handling with HTML error states and retry buttons
- Performance optimizations: async/await, CancellationToken support, pagination
- Responsive design with desktop and mobile views
- User/Guild preview popup support in all partial views
- Inline Chart.js scripts for AJAX compatibility (no @section Scripts)
- Accessibility features: ARIA labels, semantic HTML

**Documentation:**
- Updated docs/articles/api-endpoints.md with Commands API section

## Review Status

**Code Review:** APPROVED (after 1 iteration)
**UI Review:** APPROVED (after 1 iteration)

All review feedback addressed:
- ✅ Chart.js scripts moved inline for AJAX compatibility
- ✅ 90-day date range validation added to logs endpoint
- ✅ MaxPageSize constant (100) added
- ✅ Results summary conditional (hide when TotalCount = 0)
- ✅ XML documentation added to CreateErrorHtml helper
- ✅ Chart.js updated to v4.4.1 for consistency
- ✅ AJAX-loaded partial view dependency comments added
- ✅ Design system compliance verified
- ✅ Responsive design patterns match existing pages
- ✅ Accessibility features confirmed

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify all 3 endpoints return valid HTML partial views
- [ ] Test command list endpoint loads modules, parameters, and preconditions
- [ ] Test execution logs filtering by date range, guild, search term, command name, status
- [ ] Test execution logs pagination with different page sizes (1, 10, 50, 100)
- [ ] Test execution logs date range validation (reject > 90 days)
- [ ] Test analytics endpoint with different date ranges and guild filters
- [ ] Test analytics date range validation (reject > 90 days)
- [ ] Verify Chart.js renders correctly in analytics view
- [ ] Test responsive design on mobile and desktop
- [ ] Test User/Guild preview popups work in all partial views
- [ ] Test error handling with invalid parameters
- [ ] Verify error states display retry button
- [ ] Test authorization (RequireModerator) on all endpoints

Closes #1229

  - The `FLASK_ENV` environment variable, `ENV` config key, and `app.env`
    property are removed.
  - The `session_cookie_name`, `send_file_max_age_default`, `use_x_sendfile`,
    `propagate_exceptions`, and `templates_auto_reload` properties on `app`
    are removed.
  - The `JSON_AS_ASCII`, `JSON_SORT_KEYS`, `JSONIFY_MIMETYPE`, and
    `JSONIFY_PRETTYPRINT_REGULAR` config keys are removed.
  - The `app.before_first_request` and `bp.before_app_first_request` decorators
    are removed.
  - `json_encoder` and `json_decoder` attributes on app and blueprint, and the
    corresponding `json.JSONEncoder` and `JSONDecoder` classes, are removed.
  - The `json.htmlsafe_dumps` and `htmlsafe_dump` functions are removed.
  - Calling setup methods on blueprints after registration is an error instead of a
    warning. :pr:`4997`

- Importing `escape` and `Markup` from `flask` is deprecated. Import them
  directly from `markupsafe` instead. :pr:`4996`

- The `app.got_first_request` property is deprecated. :pr:`4997`

- The `locked_cached_property` decorator is deprecated. Use a lock inside the
  decorated function if locking is needed. :issue:`4993`

- Signals are always available. `blinker>=1.6.2` is a required dependency. The
  `signals_available` attribute is deprecated. :issue:`5056`

- Signals support `async` subscriber functions. :pr:`5049`

- Remove uses of locks that could cause requests to block each other very briefly.
  :issue:`4993`

- Use modern packaging metadata with `pyproject.toml` instead of `setup.cfg`.
  :pr:`4947`

- Ensure subdomains are applied with nested blueprints. :issue:`4834`

- `config.from_file` can use `text=False` to indicate that the parser wants a
  binary file instead. :issue:`4989`

- If a blueprint is created with an empty name it raises a `ValueError`.
  :issue:`5010`

- `SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN` does not fall back to `SERVER_NAME`. The default is not
  to set the domain, which modern browsers interpret as an exact match rather than
  a subdomain match. Warnings about `localhost` and IP addresses are also removed.
  :issue:`5051`

- The `routes` command shows each rule's `subdomain` or `host` when domain
  matching is in use. :issue:`5004`

- Use postponed evaluation of annotations. :pr:`5071`

## Summary
- Add inline comment to `src/logging_config.py` explaining why SDK logging is enabled when permissions debugging is active

## Details
The `sdk_debug` logger's enabled state uses: `_log_config['debug_sdk'] or _log_config['debug_permissions']`

This coupling is intentional because permission callbacks are processed through the SDK message stream. Without documentation, future maintainers might think this is a bug rather than a design decision.

The added comment clarifies this relationship:
> Enable SDK logging when either SDK or permissions debugging is active, since permission callbacks are processed through the SDK message stream

Fixes #242

body:
## Description

Integrates nested markdown linting into the pre-commit hook so markdown code blocks are validated alongside outer markdown before commit.

**Key changes:**

- **`lint-nested-markdown.js`**: Added file argument support
  - New `resolveFilePaths()` function converts CLI args to absolute paths
  - When args provided: lint only those files (fast, for pre-commit)
  - When no args: glob scan all `.md` files (backward compatible)
  - Non-existent files skipped with warning

- **`.husky/pre-commit`**: Added nested linting step after markdownlint passes
  - Passes staged files to script
  - Fails commit on nested markdown errors

- **`.github/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md`**: Design decision documenting rationale/trade-offs

```bash
# New usage - lint specific files (pre-commit)
node .github/scripts/lint-nested-markdown.js README.md docs/guide.md

# Original usage - scan all files (unchanged)
npm run lint:md:nested
```

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

## Additional Notes

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Enhance Nested Markdown Linting in Pre-commit Hook</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Context
> 
> This repository uses a Husky pre-commit hook (`pre-commit`) that currently only runs `markdownlint-cli2` on staged markdown files. We also have a script `lint-nested-markdown.js` that lints markdown code blocks within markdown files (nested markdown), but it's only available via `npm run lint:md:nested` and is not integrated into the pre-commit hook.
> 
> ## Current State
> 
> 1. **Pre-commit hook** (`pre-commit`): Only lints staged `.md` files with markdownlint-cli2
> 2. **Nested markdown script** (`lint-nested-markdown.js`): Scans all `.md` files when run manually, but does NOT accept file arguments
> 
> ## Required Changes
> 
> ### 1. Modify `lint-nested-markdown.js`
> 
> Add support for accepting file paths as command-line arguments:
> 
> - When invoked with file arguments (e.g., `node `lint-nested-markdown.js` file1.md file2.md`), lint only those specific files
> - When invoked without arguments, maintain current behavior (scan all `.md` files via glob)
> - Handle both absolute and relative paths
> - Resolve paths relative to the current working directory (where git is invoked)
> - Skip/warn if provided files don't exist
> 
> **Key implementation details:**
> 
> - Add a `resolveFilePaths()` function to convert arguments to absolute paths
> - Modify the `main()` function to check `process.argv.slice(2)` for arguments
> - Use provided files if present, otherwise fall back to glob scan
> - Update the usage documentation at the top of the file
> 
> ### 2. Update `pre-commit`
> 
> Integrate nested markdown linting for staged files:
> 
> - After the existing markdownlint check passes, run nested markdown linting on the same staged files
> - Pass `$STAGED_MD_FILES` to the script
> - Fail the commit if nested markdown linting finds errors
> - Provide clear error messaging
> 
> **Expected hook flow:**
> 
> 1. Check if there are staged markdown files
> 2. Run markdownlint-cli2 on staged files → exit 1 if fails
> 3. Run nested markdown linting on staged files → exit 1 if fails
> 4. Exit 0 if all checks pass
> 
> ### 3. Document Design Decision
> 
> Add a design decision block to `TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md` following the existing pattern used for other pre-commit documentation (see the "Conditional Pre-commit Section" around line 141).
> 
> **Location:** Add a new section in the appropriate location (likely near other pre-commit/linting documentation)
> 
> **Format:** Use HTML comment block with this structure:
> 
> ```html
> <!--
> DESIGN DECISION: [Title]
> =========================
> [Explanation of the decision]
> 
> [Numbered reasons/benefits]
> 
> TRADE-OFFS:
> [Any downsides or considerations]
> -->
> ```
> 
> **Content to document:**
> 
> - Why nested markdown linting is integrated into pre-commit (catch errors earlier)
> - Why the script was modified to accept file arguments (performance/efficiency)
> - Trade-offs (slightly slower pre-commit, but catches issues before CI)
> - Usage patterns (works with staged files only vs. full scan)
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> 
> - [ ] `lint-nested-markdown.js` accepts file arguments
> - [ ] Script maintains backward compatibility (no args = scan all files)
> - [ ] `pre-commit` runs nested markdown linting on staged files
> - [ ] Pre-commit fails if nested markdown issues are found
> - [ ] Design decision documented in `TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md` using HTML comment format
> - [ ] Design decision explains rationale, benefits, and trade-offs
> - [ ] All changes follow existing code/documentation patterns in the repository</issue_description>

### Motivation

- Implement a production-ready MVP for a viral-first, social-friendly “virtual clickable menu” that captures order requests (no payments/delivery) and maps closely to the existing supply→request→action architecture. 
- Provide three surfaces (public Storefront, Merchant portal, Admin console) so merchants can manage menus and receive order requests without building a full website. 
- Ensure the app is testable and deployable before Supabase is configured by including a mock/demo mode and copy/paste SQL for easy Supabase onboarding.

### Description

- Scaffolded an Express server with public, merchant, and admin API routes (storefront menu, combined menu, order creation, merchant login/items/orders management, admin stores/orders/summary) in `server.js`. 
- Added JWT-based auth middleware for `merchant` and `admin` roles and admin env-based login in `services/auth.js`. 
- Implemented `services/supabase.js` which supports both real Supabase (when `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are set) and an in-memory mock mode with realistic demo data, plus media upload handling to the `menu-media` bucket. 
- Built three dark-themed, premium front-end apps in plain HTML/CSS/Vanilla JS at `/apps` (storefront, merchant, admin) plus shared helpers in `public/assets/js` and styling in `public/assets/css/shared.css`. 
- Added README, `.env.example`, `supabase_schema.sql` (full SQL schema), and `package.json` to document setup, env vars, Supabase schema, and quick-start instructions.

Go-rpm-macros package requires golang to be built, but in the spec file it doesn't specify the version, so it will fetch the latest golang version available. However, the caddy spec file has limited the golang version to be between >= 1.24.4 and <1.25. This caused two golang versions to be installed here when doing delta build targeted for caddy. The go-rpm-macros has to be rebuilt instead of downloading the rpm from our repository during delta build. The same issue can be recreated using SRPM_PACK_LIST="caddy go-rpm-macros" PACKAGE_REBUILD_LIST="caddy go-rpm-macros" flag in a normal build, without the delta build flag. ### Motivation

author: copilot
body:
### What is the goal of this PR and why is this important?

Replace the existing `view_count`, `print_count`, and `download_count` counter cache columns with Ahoy event tracking to enable time-filtered analytics on the admin dashboard. The counter caches lack timestamps, making time-based analytics impossible. This PR completely removes the counter cache infrastructure and migrates to Ahoy as the single source of truth for all analytics data.

**Dependencies:** This PR depends on the Ahoy infrastructure base PR that adds the ahoy_matey gem, Ahoy::Visit and Ahoy::Event models, initializer, and database migrations. That base PR must be merged first before this PR can function.

### How did you approach the change?

**Counter Cache Removal**
- Removed `ViewCountable` and `PrintCountable` concerns from all models
- Removed `view_count`, `print_count`, and `download_count` columns from 10 models (workshops, resources, stories, events, community_news, facilitators, projects, quotes, tutorials, workshop_variations)
- Removed all `increment_view_count!`, `increment_print_count!`, and `increment!(:download_count)` calls from controllers
- Removed `by_most_viewed` scopes from all models
- Removed obsolete spec file `spec/models/concerns/view_countable_spec.rb`
- Updated system tests to use Ahoy events instead of counter cache columns
- Created migration to drop counter cache columns and their indexes

**UI & Filtering**
- Added time period dropdown to analytics view with auto-submit (all time, past day, past week, past month, past year)
- Implemented time-scoped queries using Ahoy event timestamps

**Event Tracking**
- Created `AhoyViewTracking` concern for controllers with three tracking methods:
  - `track_view(resource)` - tracks page views
  - `track_print(resource)` - tracks print actions
  - `track_download(resource)` - tracks download actions
- Applied to 10 model controllers (Workshops, Resources, Stories, Events, etc.)
- Updated admin analytics print endpoint to track prints with Ahoy
- Updated resources download endpoint to track downloads with Ahoy (removed `@resource.increment!(:download_count)`)
- Event naming follows parseable format: `action.table_name_singular`
  ```ruby
  ahoy.track "view.workshop", {
    resource_type: "Workshop",
    resource_id: 123,
    resource_title: "Art Therapy Basics"
  }
  ```
- **Session-based deduplication**: Each tracking method checks the session to prevent creating duplicate events for the same action on the same resource within a single visit. Uses session keys like `ahoy_tracked_view_Workshop_ids` to ensure one event per action per resource per visit.

**Analytics Queries**
- Query Ahoy events exclusively for all analytics data
- Added helper methods:
  - `most_viewed_for_model`, `view_count_for_model` for view analytics
  - `most_printed_for_model`, `print_count_for_model` for print analytics
  - `most_downloaded_for_model`, `download_count_for_model` for download analytics
- Extract resource IDs from event properties using MySQL-compatible JSON with `Arel.sql()` for proper SQL escaping:
  ```ruby
  Arel.sql("JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(properties, '$.resource_id'))")
  ```
- **Draper decorator compatibility**: Created `decorate_with_counts` helper method that decorates records while preserving count methods. The helper:
  1. Extracts count values from model instance variables
  2. Decorates records using Draper
  3. Attaches count methods as singleton methods directly on decorator instances
  4. Returns decorated records with `view_count`, `print_count`, and `download_count` methods accessible
- Updated `Trendable` concern to calculate view counts from Ahoy events via subqueries instead of using the removed `view_count` column
- Updated dashboard controller to work without `by_most_viewed` scope
- Optimized record sorting from O(n²) to O(n) using position hash map

**Testing**
- Added comprehensive specs for `AhoyViewTracking` concern covering event creation, deduplication, session management, and all tracking methods
- Added comprehensive specs for admin analytics controller covering time filtering (including past_day), most viewed/printed/downloaded queries, zero engagement detection, summary statistics, and access control
- Updated system tests (`facilitator_searches_resources_test.rb`, `facilitator_views_popular_resources_test.rb`) to use Ahoy event tracking instead of counter cache columns
- Created Ahoy event and visit factories (`spec/factories/ahoy_events.rb`, `spec/factories/ahoy_visits.rb`) for testing
- **Spec fixes without additional gems**: Replaced deprecated `assigns()` usage with direct database queries in request specs, avoiding the need for the `rails-controller-testing` gem
- **Proper Ahoy mocking**: Controller specs use persistent session hash to enable proper deduplication testing, ensuring session-based tracking works correctly across multiple requests
- Fixed resources factory to use `find_or_create_by` for sector to avoid uniqueness validation errors
- Fixed all Rubocop linting issues (trailing whitespace)

### Anything else to add?

**Time Period Filters:**
The analytics dashboard now supports five time period filters:
- All time (default)
- Past day (last 24 hours)
- Past week (last 7 days)
- Past month (last 30 days)
- Past year (last 365 days)

**Event Naming Convention:**
All events use a consistent, parseable format: `action.table_name_singular`
- Views: `view.workshop`, `view.resource`, `view.story`, etc.
- Prints: `print.workshop`, `print.resource`, etc.
- Downloads: `download.resource`

This makes event names predictable and easy to parse programmatically.

**Event Deduplication:**
Events are deduplicated within each visit using session tracking. This prevents inflated analytics counts when users refresh pages or navigate back. The behavior mirrors the previous `ViewCountable` concern's session-based deduplication.

**Decorator Pattern Integration:**
Records returned from analytics queries are decorated using Draper decorators. Count methods (`view_count`, `print_count`, `download_count`) are dynamically attached to decorator instances using singleton methods, ensuring compatibility with the existing decorator pattern used throughout the application. This maintains backward compatibility with existing view templates.

**Testing Approach:**
Specs use direct database queries instead of the deprecated `assigns()` helper, avoiding the need for additional gems. Controller specs use a persistent session hash that maintains state across requests, enabling proper testing of session-based deduplication behavior. The mock Ahoy tracker creates actual Ahoy::Event records when `track` is called, allowing specs to verify both event creation and deduplication.

**Migration Path:**
Historical counter cache data will be lost when the migration runs. If preservation of historical data is needed, a data migration script should be created to convert existing counter values into Ahoy events before running this migration.

**Breaking Change:**
This is a breaking change that removes database columns. Any external code, reports, or queries that reference `view_count`, `print_count`, or `download_count` columns will need to be updated to query Ahoy events instead.

Events track discrete actions (page views, prints, downloads), not visits (user sessions). This distinction enables accurate per-resource analytics with time filtering capabilities.

The Ahoy infrastructure was intentionally separated into a base PR to keep this PR focused on the analytics migration. This PR builds on top of that base infrastructure.

author: copilot
body:
Non-social content types (review, email, blog, proposal, newsletter) were incorrectly defaulting to "Instagram" as the platform, causing the AI to generate platform-specific responses for content that has no associated platform.

## Changes

**`routes/chat_routes.py`**
- Modified `_generate_content_response()` to query `task_config.require_platform` from task registry instead of hardcoded set
- Platform now defaults to `'instagram'` only for social tasks; `None` for others
- Updated `_format_generated_content()` with proper task labels ("review response" vs "review")

**`services/voice_engine.py`**
- Changed `generate_expert_content()` signature: `platform: str | None = None`
- Conditionally includes "Platform:" in prompt only when platform is provided
- Handles `None` gracefully in output format instructions and fallback text

**`services/task_registry.py`**
- Explicitly set `require_platform=True` for post, caption, script, ad
- Removed redundant `require_platform=False` (dataclass default)

## Example

Before:
```python
_generate_content_response('review', {'topic': 'bad service'}, profile)
# platform='instagram' → AI generates "Instagram-ready review response"
```

After:
```python
_generate_content_response('review', {'topic': 'bad service'}, profile)
# platform=None → AI generates platform-agnostic review response
```

## Testing

Added `tests/test_platform_defaulting.py` with 12 tests covering:
- Non-social content receives `None` platform
- Social content defaults to `'instagram'` when unspecified
- Explicit platform values are respected
- All 45 existing + new tests pass

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

Content types that don't require a platform (review, email, proposal, blog, newsletter) are incorrectly defaulting to "Instagram" as the platform, causing the AI to generate "Instagram-ready" responses for non-social content.

### Screenshot Evidence
![image1](image1)

The user ran `/review their software is garbage 1 star` and received:
> "Okay, here's an **Instagram-ready** response to a 1-star review..."

This is incorrect - review responses are meant for Google Reviews, Yelp, Facebook Reviews, etc. - NOT Instagram.

## Root Cause

In `routes/chat_routes.py` line ~343, the `_generate_content_response()` function has a hardcoded default:

```python
def _generate_content_response(task_type: str, params: dict, profile: VoiceProfile) -> dict:
    try:
        topic = params.get('topic', '')
        platform = params.get('platform', 'instagram')  # 👈 BUG: Always defaults to Instagram!
        
        content = voice_engine.generate_expert_content(
            user_profile=profile,
            topic=topic,
            task_type=task_type,
            platform=platform,  # 👈 Passed to voice engine even for non-social content
            **extra_context
        )
```

This causes ALL content types to receive "instagram" as the platform, even when it doesn't make sense.

## Affected Content Types

| Task Type | Should Have Platform? | Current Behavior | Problem |
|-----------|----------------------|------------------|---------|
| `post` | ✅ Yes | Defaults to Instagram | ✅ OK (expected) |

author: joshluxr
body:
## Summary
- Transition to Terragon Platform monorepo bootstrap with API, Web, Worker, and UI, wired with Prisma, BullMQ, and production-like scaffolding
- Establishes a Terragon Platform monorepo layout (apps/api, apps/web, apps/worker, packages/database, packages/shared, packages/ui) with Docker tooling and local env examples
- Includes a production-like demo frontend, API routes, queues, sockets, sandbox abstractions, and an agent-runner scaffold
- Frontend UI, shared libraries, and a UI component library wired for a cohesive production-like demo experience
- Some components remain scaffolds/simulations to bootstrap local development, with hooks to wire real services in future iterations

## Changes
- Backend API
  - New Express TS app with Prisma integration and BullMQ-based queues
  - Core middleware: auth (JWT or API keys), error handling, rate limiting
  - Routes: /api/auth, /api/tasks, /api/integrations, /api/billing, /api/webhooks, /api/automations
  - WebSocket support via socket.io with per-user rooms and task subscriptions
  - Queues and workers bootstrap (queues/index.ts) and task processing integration
  - Sandbox service abstraction for running tasks in isolated sandboxes (stubbed for now)
  - Agent runner scaffold for multi-provider agents (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Custom)
- Worker
  - terragon-platform/apps/worker with Dockerfile, package.json, and worker entrypoint
  - Worker logic scaffold for processing tasks from the queue and simulating sandboxed work
- Database & Shared libs
  - Prisma schema and client wiring (packages/database)
  - Shared types/constants/utilities (packages/shared)
- Web UI (Next.js app)
  - terragon-platform/apps/web scaffold with Next.js 14, Tailwind, and UI library integration
  - Landing pages and dashboard UI components (header, nav, layout, etc)
  - Authentication flow wired to NextAuth (GitHub + Google), JWT-based sessions
  - API client wrapper (src/lib/api.ts) and socket hooks (src/hooks/use-socket.ts)
  - Routing, pages for dashboard, tasks, login, and docs-like pages
  - Public assets for AI agents (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Custom)
- UI Library & Components
  - Core UI components under terragon-platform/packages/ui (buttons, cards, dialogs, etc.)
  - Landing pages use cohesive UI for a production-feel demo
- Infrastructure & Config
  - terragon-platform/.env.example for local dev, docker-compose tooling to bootstrap services
  - terragon-platform/.gitignore and README.md (generated)
  - terragon-platform/turbo.json, pnpm workspace, and tsconfig setups
- Types & Auth Integration
  - Next-auth types extended to carry user data and GitHub token in JWT/session
  - API types and contract surfaces prepared for frontend usage

## How to run locally (development)
Prerequisites:
- Node.js 18+ and pnpm 8+
- Docker & Docker Compose
- GitHub OAuth App credentials (for GitHub sign-in)
- Optional Stripe keys for billing endpoints (used in frontend demo)

1) Install dependencies
- pnpm install

2) Configure environment
- Copy terragon-platform/.env.example to terragon-platform/.env and fill credentials as needed
- For local API, set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:4000 and FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:3000 in the env

3) Run infrastructure (in repo root)
- docker-compose up -d postgres redis
- Note: Prisma migrations/template would run via internal scripts during API/build as needed

4) Start backend API
- From terragon-platform/apps/api, run: pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm start
- API will listen on http://localhost:4000

5) Start frontend web UI
- From terragon-platform/apps/web, run: pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm start
- UI will be available at http://localhost:3000

6) Optional: Start worker
- From terragon-platform/apps/worker, run: pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm start
- Worker will process tasks queued by the API

7) Optional: Run with Docker Compose
- docker-compose -f terragon-platform/docker-compose.yml up -d
- Access API at http://localhost:4000 and UI at http://localhost:3000

## Testing / Validation plan
- Smoke test the auth flow via the web UI (GitHub login mocked in dev)
- Create a task from the frontend and verify the following lifecycle:
  - Task goes to QUEUED then RUNNING in backend
  - Logs and progress events are emitted via Socket.IO
  - Sandbox is created (simulated by sandbox service) and agent steps emit logs
  - If changes exist, a mock PR URL is produced and task status becomes COMPLETED
  - Credits deduction is recorded in the database
- Validate integrations page can list Slack/GitHub connectors and Slack webhook path can be saved
- Verify billing endpoints respond (checkout/portal) with mock responses when Stripe keys are configured
- Verify frontend API wrapper can fetch current user, tasks, and task details; CRUD flows for tasks work end-to-end (using mocked data in this scaffold)

## Notes / Caveats
- This PR scaffolds the Terragon Platform end-to-end architecture for TerragonLabs replication. While the codebase is wired for many features (auth, queues, sandbox, agent runners), some pieces are implemented as scaffolds/simulations (e.g., sandbox execution and PR creation) and should be connected to real services in later iterations.
- Environment variables and external service integrations (Stripe, GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) require proper credentials to be fully functional.
- The Prisma schema and database migrations are included in the diff as scaffolding; adjust migrations for your deployment strategy.

## Migration / Upgrade considerations
- This is a bootstrap integration introducing a new monorepo layout. If you already have a database, ensure Prisma schema matches your data models and run appropriate migrations before deploying.
- Frontend and backend communicate via JWTs and API keys; ensure proper secret management in production.
- The sandbox/agent runner currently uses a simulation pathway. Replace with real sandbox provisioning and agent execution in a follow-up change.

⚡ Bolt: Add database indexes to todos table

💡 What: Added B-tree indexes to `createdAt` and `completed` columns in `todos` table.
🎯 Why: The `findAll` query orders by `createdAt` descending and often filters by `completed`. Without indexes, these operations perform full table scans/sorts.
📊 Impact: Transforms O(N log N) sorting and O(N) filtering into O(log N) operations.
🔬 Measurement: Verify via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a populated database or check generated migration file `0002_lowly_wrecking_crew.sql`.

### Motivation
- Visa portal parser previously built `raw` objects only from detected header map keys, which can omit original header labels that contain installment counts and prevent the UI from showing installment suffixes like `(2/10)`.

### Description
- Updated `server/ingest/parsers/creditCardVisaPortalParser.js` to capture the full header row labels into a `headerLabels` array when the header is detected.
- When building the `raw` object for each data row, the parser now prefers the `headerLabels` mapping (mapping each header label to the corresponding cell) so all original column names and values are preserved.
- Kept the previous behavior as a fallback by still populating `raw` from `headerMap` if `headerLabels` is not available.

author: josher8a
body:
## Summary

  - **Type-level performance** — fused and simplified core types (`CompositeKeyBuilder`, `SliceFromStart`, `ExtractHelper`, `ProcessVariant`, `TableEntryImpl`, `Exact`) to reduce
  TypeScript instantiation counts across the board
  - **`.key()` attribute narrowing** — transforms now narrow their parameter types (e.g. `Pick<A, 'w'>` instead of full `A`), with contravariant intersection when the same key appears
  in multiple spec positions
  - **Error diagnostics** — invalid schemas and specs surface `ErrorMessage<"...">` in the IDE instead of opaque `never`; empty separator is a compile-time error; all runtime errors
  throw `RotoriseError`
  - **Publish hygiene** — `files: ["dist"]`, `treeshake: true`, removed `@swc/jest`

  ## Breaking Changes

  - `Exact` only checks top-level excess properties (no deep recursion)
  - `.key()` attributes narrow to transform parameter types
  - Schema keys on `TableEntry` are `readonly`
  - Invalid schemas return `ErrorMessage<>` instead of `never`

Fixes #3589

This PR updates the iOS "Logs" knowledge section (`MASTG-KNOW-0101`) to provide a more complete and realistic view of the iOS logging ecosystem. Previously, the test focused primarily on Apple's Unified Logging System, while in practice sensitive data is often leaked through additional, less obvious logging channels.

This update expands coverage to include these real-world sources and adds concrete test guidance to help testers identify unintended log exposure during assessments.

**Changes:**
- **Expanded logging coverage**
  - Added logging via `stdout` / `stderr` (e.g., `print`, `printf`, C/C++ output)
  - Documented legacy `NSLog` behavior and associated risks
  - Added WebView JavaScript console logging (`console.log`)
  - Covered third-party SDK and crash reporting logs

- **Improved test steps**
  - Added dynamic inspection steps using **Console.app**
  - Added CLI-based log inspection using `xcrun simctl log`
  - Included guidance on filtering by process and bundle identifier

- **Remediation guidance**
  - Added secure logging recommendations using `os_log` privacy modifiers
  - Added guidance for stripping debug logs in Release builds
  - Included mitigation steps for WebView and third-party SDK logging

- **Formatting & consistency**
  - Aligned structure with MASTG v2 test conventions
  - Fixed code block formatting and added language specifiers
  - Updated references to official Apple documentation

**Verification:**

## 変更内容

# 変更前
from claude_generator import (

author: mahdisadjadi
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Mahdisadjadi/arxivscraper/issues/28

## Summary
This PR addresses a critical bug where invalid arXiv categories returned the integer `1` instead of an error, and adds support for missing categories (`cs`, `econ`, `eess`) that were not recognized by the scraper.

## Changes

### Bug Fixes

1. **Fixed exception handling in `scrape()` method**
   - Changed line 218 in `arxivscraper.py` from `return 1` to `return ds`
   - Previously, when an exception occurred while parsing the resumption token, the method would return the integer `1` instead of the accumulated records list
   - This caused silent failures for invalid categories with no clear error message

2. **Added category validation**
   - New `_validate_category()` method in `Scraper.__init__`
   - Validates category names upfront and raises `ValueError` with helpful error messages
   - Supports both `:` and `.` separators for subcategories (e.g., `cs:SE` and `cs.SE`)
   - Prevents confusing integer return values by failing fast with clear error messages

### Feature Additions

3. **Added missing arXiv categories to constants.py**
   - Added base categories: `cs`, `econ`, `eess`
   - Added all 41 Computer Science subcategories (cs.AI, cs.SE, etc.)
   - Added Economics subcategories (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH)
   - Added Electrical Engineering and Systems Science subcategories (eess.AS, eess.IV, eess.SP, eess.SY)
   - Categories sourced from arXiv's official taxonomy

4. **Updated .gitignore**
   - Added `.DS_Store` to prevent macOS system files from being tracked

### Testing

5. **Comprehensive category validation tests** (`tests/test_category_validation.py`)
   - `test_valid_base_category`: Verifies all base categories are accepted
   - `test_valid_subcategory`: Tests both `:` and `.` subcategory separators
   - `test_invalid_category_raises_error`: Confirms invalid categories raise `ValueError`
   - `test_cs_se_category_specifically`: Explicitly tests the category from the issue
   - `test_error_message_helpful`: Validates error messages list available categories

body:
### Motivation

- Preserve original engine behavior and initialization order while porting core systems to Java 25 for deterministic parity.  
- Provide a clear platform GPU targeting strategy that supports Apple Silicon (M2/ARM), Windows and Linux/ARM to guide backend implementations.  
- Establish minimal contracts for procedural, audio and rendering subsystems so platform-specific implementations can be developed independently.  

### Description

- Document migration order and platform GPU targets in `java25/README.md` and add local run/build instructions using `./gradlew :java25:build`.  
- Add platform utilities `PlatformTarget` and `PlatformSelector` to select a default GPU backend based on `os.name` and `os.arch`.  
- Introduce core contracts `ProceduralPipeline`, `AudioEngine`, and `RenderBackend` and a coordinator `EngineBootstrap` that enforces the original initialization sequence.  
- Add foundational Java 25 modules and primitives including `FixedMath`, `FixedVector3`, `GpuBuffer` (FFM-based off-heap buffer), and Gradle configuration files (`build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts`).  

### Testing

# Audit Event Logging Gaps and Implement Lifecycle Events

## Description
Implements the "Facts on the Ground" event lifecycle as detailed in `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW.md`. This ensures that all significant user actions (Media Upload, AI Analysis, Voice Capture) are recorded as distinct events, even if the final "Log Entry" save fails or is incomplete.

### Key Changes
-   **Store Schema**: Added `mediaIds` to `LogEntry` to link entries to their media lifecycle events.
-   **Media Lifecycle**: Refactored `log/+page.svelte` to dispatch `media/uploadStarted` immediately upon selection, and `media/uploadCompleted` or `media/uploadFailed` asynchronously.
-   **AI Lifecycle**: Wrapped Gemini analysis calls in `log/+page.svelte` with `ai/analysisRequested` and `ai/analysisFailed` events.
-   **Voice Lifecycle**: Updated `VoiceRecorder.svelte` to dispatch `voice/captureCompleted` with raw transcript and duration before analysis.

## Original User Prompt
> Read DEVELOPMENT.md and designs/DESIGN_REVIEW.md. Implement the ideas in the design review and then follow WORKFLOW.md to create a PR.

## Verification

author: songka
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure TTS is reliable and uses the exact required wording and pacing (slow ID/name) and never blocks the state machine on error. 
- Make automatic multi-draw exhaust the remaining slots of the current prize using a preview state to avoid duplicates. 
- Prevent target jumping during braking by locking the active target and implement monotonic deceleration so the pointer never speeds up or mis-targets. 
- Improve wheel label legibility and the grand-summary layout (waterfall columns) and disable start when a prize has no remaining slots.

### Description
- TTS: removed reuse of a shared engine and initialize `pyttsx3.init()` per-speech in `_speak_winner`, speak the exact phrase `"恭喜，{工号}，{姓名}，获得，{奖项}"` with slow `rate` for ID/name (spaced digits) and faster for the prize, print exceptions with `print("TTS error:", e)`, always call `engine.stop()` if present, and always set `self.tts_done_event` in `finally` to avoid flow deadlocks. 
- Multi-draw preview: replaced single-call draw with a loop in `_start_draw_logic` that runs `draw_prize` against a `preview_state` up to `remaining` times, accumulates `winners_list`, writes each winner into `preview_state` to prevent duplicates, then fills `pending_winners`/`target_queue` from the accumulated list. 
- Target lock & braking physics: added `self.active_target_id` and set it when spinning transitions to braking; `_calculate_stop_path_by_time` uses the locked id; braking now uses a monotonic deceleration model (`a = 0.35 + 1.2 * locked_charge`, `v_limit = sqrt(2*a*dist)`, decrement `current_speed` by `a` each frame) and stops when `dist_remaining < 0.2` or `current_speed == 0` to avoid instantaneous jumps or speed-ups. 
- Stop/announcement flow: `_handle_stop` uses the locked `active_target_id` (pops the queue conservatively), always calls `_speak_winner` before starting removal and refreshes prize options after applying a winner to keep `prize_var` options synchronized. 
- Wheel rendering and summary: fixed pointer hit test to `min(abs(mid_angle-90), 360-abs(mid_angle-90))`; extended `_draw_text_with_outline` to accept `angle` and replaced raw `create_text` on segments with outlined rotated text for better contrast; changed grand-summary to a waterfall layout (place each prize block into the shortest column) and adjusted `summary_scroll_margin` for adaptive scrolling. 
- UX guards: added `_current_prize_remaining()` and checks in `_on_input_down` and `_update_btn_state` to disable/return early when a prize has no remaining slots.

author: copilot
body:
Built a static analyzer MVP for Zig with plugin-based architecture supporting arbitrary linting rules. Implements initial rule detecting empty `catch {}` blocks, a common anti-pattern that silently discards errors.

## Architecture

**Core components:**
- `analyzer.zig` - File I/O, rule orchestration, violation aggregation
- `rule.zig` - `Rule` interface using function pointers for zero-overhead polymorphism
- `main.zig` - CLI with standard error reporting format `file:line:col: rule: message`

**Extensibility model:**
```zig
// Add rule in src/rules/new_rule.zig
pub const NewRule = struct {
    pub const rule: Rule = Rule{
        .name = "rule-name",
        .checkFn = check,
    };
    
    fn check(source: []const u8, file_path: []const u8, 
             violations: *std.ArrayList(Violation)) !void {
        // Implementation
    }
};

// Register in main.zig
try analyzer.registerRule(&NewRule.rule);
```

## Empty Catch Rule

Detects both `catch {}` and `catch |err| {}` patterns. Handles:
- Whitespace variations
- Multiple violations per file  
- Malformed code (missing braces/pipes) without crashing
- Accurate line/column tracking

**Example violation:**
```zig
const file = openFile("data.txt") catch {}; // Flagged
const file = openFile("data.txt") catch |err| {
    log.err("Failed to open: {}", .{err});
    return err;
}; // OK
```

## Memory safety

All allocations paired with `defer` cleanup, array accesses bounds-checked. No unsafe operations.

## Testing

Unit tests cover positive/negative cases and malformed input. Examples in `examples/` demonstrate violations and fixes.

author: norepro
body:
Extracting files uses the filename to determine the MIME type and thus the crates to invoke for extracting the file. This causes an error if the file has an incorrect extension, e.g., `.tar` instead of `.tar.gz`.

Fixing the file extension works, but it is a bad user experience, especially compared to other file managers (Dolphin, Nautilus) and utilities (tar) that succeed in the same scenario.

When extracting a file, try to determine the file type by looking at its magic bytes. If that logic fails for any reason, fallback to the filename logic.

Checking magic bytes is technically slower than simple path logic, but this is only invoked on a single file when the user has confirmed they want to extract it anyway. This logic is _not_ used in any other scenario, e.g. determining icons to show.

Fixes #1522

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary
Stub enhancement for Erdős Problem #362: Subset Sum Concentration.

This problem asks whether the number of subsets of a finite set summing to a fixed target is bounded by O(2^N/N^{3/2}), and with fixed subset size, by O(2^N/N^2). Both questions were answered affirmatively by Sárközy-Szemerédi (1965) and Halász (1977).

## Changes
- Rewrote Lean proof with proper formalization of subset sum counting
- Defined `subsetSumsTo`, `subsetSumCount`, `restrictedSubsetSumCount`, `maxSubsetSumCount`
- Axiomatized Sárközy-Szemerédi theorem (first question) and Halász theorem (second question)
- Added Stanley's extremal result and connection to Littlewood-Offord problem
- Verified concrete examples for small sets ({1,2,3}, {1,2,3,4}) via `native_decide`
- Updated meta.json with historical context, key insights, and proper mathlib dependencies
- Created annotations.json with 12 educational annotations covering all major sections

body:
## What（何を変更したか）

Anthropicの公式スキル作成ベストプラクティスに基づき、6つのClaude Codeコマンドファイルを大幅に改善しました。

- **commit-and-pr.md**: 7ステップの詳細なワークフローを追加、`gh pr view --web`を追加
- **commit.md**: 5ステップのワークフローとConventional Commitsガイドラインを追加
- **enrich-issue.md**: フェーズ見出しを日本語化、対話的な充実化プロセスを明確化
- **fix-issue.md**: 重複した2つのワークフローを統合し、単一の包括的な9ステップワークフローに改善、EnterPlanModeとIssueコメント追跡を追加
- **format-issue.md**: 6ステップのワークフローと変換例を追加
- **tidying.md**: Kent BeckのTidy First原則に基づく包括的な6ステップワークフローを追加（15行から140行へ拡充）

## Why（なぜ変更が必要だったか）

既存のコマンドファイルは簡潔すぎて、Claudeが効果的に実行するには不十分でした。特に以下の問題がありました:

1. **Description フィールドが不明確**: 三人称で記述されておらず、トリガーとなるキーワードが含まれていない
2. **ワークフローが不足**: ステップバイステップの手順やチェックリストがない
3. **フィードバックループが欠如**: テスト駆動や検証のプロセスが明示されていない
4. **重複コンテンツ**: fix-issue.mdに2つの異なるワークフローが存在し、一貫性がない
5. **言語の混在**: 英語と日本語が一貫性なく混在

この変更により、Claudeがコマンドを正確に理解・実行し、ユーザーが進捗を追跡しやすくなります。

## 🔗 Related Issues

該当なし

## 💡 Discussion Points / Technical Concerns

- **ハイブリッド言語方式**: Descriptionは英語（Claudeの理解向上のため）、本文は日本語（ユーザーの可読性のため）としました
- **詳細度のバランス**: 一部のファイル（特にtidying.md）が大幅に拡充されましたが、必要な情報を網羅するために必要と判断しました
- **fix-issue.mdの統合**: 2つの異なるワークフロー（6ステップと8ステップ）を9ステップの単一ワークフローに統合しましたが、重要な要素はすべて保持されています

body:
### Motivation
- Surface discovered code components and track rent-manifest coverage so newly-discovered modules can be reviewed and admitted or flagged before they are relied on in production. 
- Provide an auditable approval ledger and rune-adaptation drafts to close the loop between discovered components and capability/rune registrations. 
- Improve cryptographic receipts by adding an Ed25519 signing backend for governance artifacts when keys are configured. 

### Description
- Added a server-side governance registry at `server/governance/component-registry.ts` and exposed endpoints `GET /api/governance/component-registry` and `POST /api/governance/component-approvals` via `server/routes.ts` to return discovery data and record approvals with reviewer attribution.  
- Implemented a client UI and bindings: `client/src/pages/GovernanceRegistry.tsx`, API helpers `fetchComponentRegistry` and `postComponentApproval` in `client/src/api.ts`, integrated the page into `client/src/App.tsx`, and added a sidebar item in `client/src/components/app-sidebar.tsx`.  
- Extended Python manifest tooling in `abraxas/governance/rent_manifest_loader.py` with `discover_component_registry`, `find_unmanifested_components`, and `_discover_modules_in_dir` to discover modules and diff them against rent manifests; added a correspondingly-updated test in `tests/test_rent_enforcement.py`.  
- Implemented Ed25519 sign/verify in `shared/signing.py` using `cryptography` with env-configured base64 keys and added `cryptography` to `pyproject.toml`; added deterministic golden fixtures under `tests/golden/` and updated docs (`docs/specs/rent_enforcement_v0_1.md`) and frontend deps (`package.json` / `package-lock.json`) for YAML handling and registry features.  
- Minor housekeeping: removed a stale TODO note from `CLAUDE.md` and adjusted a small metric registry comment.  

### Testing
- Updated unit test `tests/test_rent_enforcement.py` to call `discover_component_registry` and `find_unmanifested_components` and assert unmanifested modules are a subset of discovered registry entries.  
- Added deterministic golden files `tests/golden/forecast/ensemble_deepfake_H72H.json` and `tests/golden/scoreboard/score_H72H_summary.json` to support manifest proof checks used by tests.

author: cpj2195
body:
This PR adds AWS Auto Scaling Group (ASG) support for roachprod, mirroring the existing GCE Managed Instance Group (MIG) implementation. Managed clusters enable dynamic cluster resizing via roachprod grow and roachprod shrink
operations.

Summary

Add --aws-managed flag to create clusters using Launch Templates and Auto Scaling Groups
Implement Grow() and Shrink() operations for managed AWS clusters
Implement proper cleanup of ASG, launch templates, and load balancer resources on cluster destroy
AWS ASG doesn't support creating instances with custom names (unlike GCE MIG which has create-instance --instance ). To preserve roachprod's naming conventions (e.g., clustername-0001, clustername-0002), we:

Create the launch template (stores instance configuration)
Create the ASG with desiredCapacity=0 (management structure only)
Create instances using runInstance() with proper names
Attach instances to the ASG using attach-instances
This approach maintains compatibility with roachprod's cluster naming while gaining ASG benefits for grow/shrink operations.

For managed clusters, target groups are attached directly to the ASG using attach-load-balancer-target-groups. This provides:

Automatic instance registration: New instances launched or attached to the ASG are automatically registered with the target group
Automatic deregistration: Instances removed from the ASG are automatically deregistered
Simplified grow operations: No need for manual register-targets calls when adding nodes
Resource Naming

Launch Template: {cluster}-lt
Auto Scaling Group: {cluster}-{region}-asg
Epic: None
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/153071

author: copilot
body:
Implements a Python consumer for Solace topics that outputs messages with running count.

## Implementation

**Core consumer** (`solace_consumer.py`, 186 lines)
- `MessageCounter` class handles async message callbacks via Solace `MessageHandler` interface
- Displays message number, topic, payload for each received message
- Tracks cumulative count, outputs total on graceful shutdown

**Configuration** 
- CLI arguments via argparse: `--host`, `--vpn`, `--username`, `--password`, `--topic`
- Falls back to environment variables (`SOLACE_HOST`, etc.), then hardcoded defaults
- Username masked in logs to avoid credential exposure

**Payload handling**
- Attempts string payload first, falls back to UTF-8 decode of bytes
- Handles empty strings, binary data, decode failures gracefully

**Error handling**
- Null-safe cleanup for partial initialization failures
- Exception wrapping for receiver termination and disconnect

## Usage

```bash
# With CLI args
python solace_consumer.py --host tcp://broker:55555 --topic "events/>"

# With env vars
export SOLACE_HOST="tcp://broker:55555"
export SOLACE_TOPIC="events/>"
python solace_consumer.py
```

Output format:
```
============================================================
Message #1
Topic: events/user/login
Payload: {"userId": 123, "timestamp": "2026-01-19T07:24:00Z"}
============================================================
Total messages received: 1
```

**Dependencies**: `solace-pubsubplus==1.5.0`

⚡ Bolt: Optimized search index generation in Sidebar

💡 What:
Changed the string concatenation logic in `Sidebar.tsx` to perform `.toLowerCase()` once on the combined string `(name + " " + domain).toLowerCase()` instead of calling it on each part individually.

🎯 Why:
To reduce intermediate string allocations during the `searchIndex` generation. For N cases, this reduces allocations from 3*N to 2*N (approx) and avoids creating intermediate lowercase strings that are immediately discarded. While a micro-optimization, it adheres to the philosophy of making the code more efficient where low-hanging fruit exists.

- Reduces string allocations during Sidebar initialization/refresh.

author: copilot
body:
The philosophical reasoning system was returning empty analysis structures (`Perspectives: [], Principles: [], Considerations: [], Conflicts: []`) for ethical dilemmas like the trolley problem. Root cause: `WorldModelToolWrapper` intercepted philosophical queries and returned template responses instead of calling the world model's actual reasoning pipeline.

## Changes

### World Model Core (`world_model_core.py`)
- **Added ethical dilemma detection**: `_is_ethical_dilemma()` pattern-matches trolley problems, life/death scenarios, choice structures, moral principles
- **Added 5-phase analysis pipeline**: `_analyze_ethical_dilemma()` parses structure → extracts principles → analyzes options → detects conflicts → synthesizes decision
- **Updated routing**: `_philosophical_reasoning()` now checks for external dilemmas first, routes to analysis pipeline

### Tool Selector Integration (`tool_selector.py`) 
- **Critical fix**: Added `_apply_philosophical_reasoning_from_world_model()` which calls `world_model._philosophical_reasoning()` directly
- **Removed template fallbacks**: System now returns authentic reasoning from Vulcan's meta-reasoning components (MotivationalIntrospection, EthicalBoundaryMonitor, GoalConflictDetector) or error state—no synthetic responses
- **Enhanced routing**: `_determine_aspect_and_query()` detects ethical dilemmas (≥2 indicators) before self-referential checks

## Example

Before:
```python
result = world_model._philosophical_reasoning(trolley_query)
# { 'perspectives': [], 'principles': [], 'conflicts': [], ... }
```

After:
```python
result = world_model._philosophical_reasoning(trolley_query)
# {
#   'perspectives': ['consequentialist', 'deontological'],
#   'principles': ['non-instrumentalization', 'non-negligence'],
#   'considerations': ['Option A: Pull lever - Complies: non-negligence...'],

This empty output indicates the `_philosophical_reasoning` method is **not analyzing external ethical dilemmas** - it only handles self-referential queries about the AI itself.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Issue 1: `_philosophical_reasoning` Only Handles Self-Referential Queries

Looking at `src/vulcan/reasoning/selection/tool_selector.py` (WorldModelToolWrapper class), the `_get_philosophical_analysis` method only has analysis templates for:

author: shaw-baobao
body:
## Problem

The stop button was not working when trying to cancel a conversation immediately after sending a message.

## Root Cause

`canInterrupt` required both `isProcessing` AND `activeTurnId` to be truthy:
```typescript
const canInterrupt = activeThreadId
  ? Boolean(
      threadStatusById[activeThreadId]?.isProcessing &&
        activeTurnIdByThread[activeThreadId]
    )
  : false;
```

However, `activeTurnId` is only set after the server responds to the turn start request. This means users couldn't stop the request during the initial network delay.

## Solution

1. Simplify `canInterrupt` to only check `isProcessing` state
2. Move the `activeTurnId` check in `interruptTurn` after UI state updates, so the UI reflects the stopped state even when `turnId` isn't available yet

## Testing

Tested locally - the stop button now works immediately after sending a message.

body:
Fixed the error: "Failed to execute 'drawImage' on 'CanvasRenderingContext2D': The provided value is not of type '(CSSImageValue or HTMLCanvasElement or HTMLImageElement or HTMLVideoElement or ImageBitmap or OffscreenCanvas or SVGImageElement or VideoFrame)'."

The issue occurred in three encoding functions (encodeFramesWithCanvas, encodeFramesWithGif, encodeFramesWithEncoder) when frames were passed as objects like { frame: ImageData, clip: ClipInfo } instead of raw frame data.

The fallback code now properly handles:
1. Direct ImageData objects (uses putImageData)
2. Object frames with .frame property (extracts and handles the actual frame)
3. Other valid CanvasImageSource types (uses drawImage)

This prevents the type error when video processing operations encounter wrapped frame objects.

author: copilot
body:
## Proposed Changes

XSS vulnerability in comment URL field allows arbitrary JavaScript execution when malicious URLs are submitted. Attack payload like `http://baidu/"onfocus="location.href='https://evil.com'"autofocus="">` contains quotes that break out of href attributes to inject event handlers.

- **Enhanced `Common::safeUrl()` function** in `var/Typecho/Common.php` to remove dangerous characters (`"`, `'`, `<`, `>`) during input validation
- **Input-level filtering**: Dangerous characters are removed when users submit comments, **before** data is stored in the database
- **Centralized protection**: Fix applies to all entry points (comment submission, comment editing, trackbacks) through the `url` filter
- **Defense in depth**: Sanitized data in database + DOMPurify as secondary layer

**Before** (vulnerable):
```php
$params = array_map(function ($string) {
    $string = str_replace(['%0d', '%0a'], '', strip_tags($string));
    return preg_replace([
        "/\(\s*([\"'])/i",
        "/([\"'])\s*\)/i",
    ], '', $string);
}, $params);
```

**After** (secure):
```php
$params = array_map(function ($string) {
    $string = str_replace(['%0d', '%0a'], '', strip_tags($string));
    $string = preg_replace([
        "/\(\s*([\"'])/i",
        "/([\"'])\s*\)/i",
    ], '', $string);
    // Remove quotes and other dangerous characters that could be used for XSS attacks
    $string = str_replace(['"', "'", '<', '>'], '', $string);
    return $string;
}, $params);
```

**Example:**
- Input: `http://baidu/"onfocus="location.href='https://typecho.work'"autofocus="">666`
- Output: `http://baidu/onfocus=location.href=https://typecho.workautofocus=666`
- Result: All quotes removed → Cannot break out of HTML attributes → XSS prevented at source

Affects Typecho 1.2.1 and 1.3.0-dev. 4 lines changed in `var/Typecho/Common.php`.

### Vert.x Web static handler component cache can be manipulated to deny the access to static files
[CVE-2026-1002](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-1002) / [GHSA-cphf-4846-3xx9](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cphf-4846-3xx9)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The Vert.x Web static handler component cache can be manipulated to deny the access to static files served by the handler using specifically crafted request URI.

The issue comes from an improper implementation of the C. rule of section 5.2.4 of RFC3986 and is fixed in Vert.x Core component (used by Vert.x Web):  [https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/pull/5895](https://redirect.github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/pull/5895) 

Steps to reproduce
Given a file served by the static handler, craft an URI that introduces a string like bar%2F..%2F after the last / char to deny the access to the URI with an HTTP 404 response. For example https://example.com/foo/index.html can be denied with https://example.com/foo/bar%2F..%2Findex.html

Mitgation
Disabling Static Handler cache fixes the issue.

StaticHandler staticHandler = StaticHandler.create().setCachingEnabled(false);

- CVSS Score: 6.9 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:L`
