### Vert.x has a DoS via unbounded server-side SNI SslContext cache growth
[CVE-2026-6860](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-6860) / [GHSA-3g76-f9xq-8vp6](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g76-f9xq-8vp6)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
Potential unbounded server-side SNI `SslContext` cache growth in Vert.x TLS handling, with = resource-exhaustion / DoS impact. On affected versions, matching server-side SNI names are cached via `computeIfAbsent(serverName, ...)` in a serverName-keyed `SslContext` cache.

The implementation differs slightly by branch, but the same sink appears to be present in released versions `4.3.4` through `5.0.11`:
- `4.3.x`: `SSLHelper`
- `4.4.x` / `4.5.x`: `SslChannelProvider`
- `5.0.x` and current `master`: `SslContextProvider`

When server-side SNI is enabled and wildcard or otherwise broad hostname mappings are used, an unauthenticated client can send many distinct matching SNI names and cause the server to retain increasing numbers of `SslContext` entries over time, leading to increasing memory consumption and possible DoS conditions.

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Vert.x server with `setSsl(true)` and `setSni(true)`.
2. Use a keystore or mapping where many distinct SNI names match a wildcard or similarly broad rule.
3. Send repeated connections with distinct matching SNI values.
4. Observe that the SNI cache size grows with the number of unique matching names.

##### What are the affected versions?

Affected released versions confirmed on `origin`:
- `4.3.4` through `4.3.8`
- `4.4.0` through `4.4.9`
- `4.5.0` through `4.5.26`
- `5.0.0` through `5.0.11`

Not affected by the same sink:
- `4.0.x` through `4.2.x`
- `4.3.0` through `4.3.3`

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.9 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:L`

body:
## 概要

このPRは、setup.shのワークフロー変更に対応するため、e2eテストにGitリポジトリ初期化処理を追加します。

setup.shがGitリポジトリ内での実行を前提とするようになったため、テスト用の一時ディレクトリでもGitリポジトリの初期化が必要になりました。

## 変更内容

### 🐛 バグ修正

- e2eテストがsetup.shのワークフロー変更後に失敗する問題を修正
- すべてのe2eテストファイルにGitリポジトリ初期化処理を追加

### ✨ 新機能

- `tests/helpers/common.bash`に新しいヘルパー関数`init_test_git_repo()`を追加
  - テストディレクトリをGitリポジトリとして初期化
  - テスト用のgitユーザー設定
  - 初期コミットの作成
  - ダミーのoriginリモートを追加
  - developブランチの作成とチェックアウト

## 技術的詳細

### 問題の原因

setup.shは以下の条件を必要とするようになりました：
1. Gitリポジトリ内で実行されること
2. originリモートが設定されていること
3. developブランチが存在すること

### 解決策

`init_test_git_repo()`ヘルパー関数を作成し、以下の処理を行います：

```bash
init_test_git_repo() {
    local target_dir="$1"
    (
        cd "$target_dir" || return 1
        git init -q
        git config user.email "test@example.com"
        git config user.name "Test User"
        touch .gitkeep
        git add .gitkeep
        git commit -q -m "Initial commit for test"
        git remote add origin "https://github.com/test/test-repo.git"
        git checkout -q -b develop
    )
}
```

### 変更されたファイル

- `tests/helpers/common.bash` - 新しいヘルパー関数を追加

- `tests/e2e/test_docker_option.bats`

author: jonrandahl
body:
**Deploy Target:** Prod (Release)

> [!TIP]
> This is a release PR. All changes have been reviewed and merged
> into `dev`. Approval confirms the version and changes are ready for testing
> before production release.

## Summary

Modernised the front-end stack by migrating from deprecated Ruby Sass
(`sass-rails` / `bootstrap-sass`) to Dart Sass with Bootstrap 5 support,
resolved gem versioning warnings, and improved UI/UX across the application.

Relates to #308, #309, #312

## Changes

- Replaced `bootstrap-sass` with `bootstrap` gem for Dart Sass compatibility
- Added `dartsass-sprockets` gem for Rails integration
- Updated stylesheets to use Sass modules (`@use 'sass:color'` instead of deprecated `lighten`)
- Removed `sass-rails` gem and deprecated dependencies
- Modernised modals and forms to Bootstrap 5 notation (`data-bs-dismiss` attributes)
- Converted form groups to semantic fieldsets for improved accessibility
- Enhanced error page layout with additional status messages (403, 422)
- Improved page layout padding and form spacing
- Enhanced action buttons responsiveness with flexbox
- Added cookie banner styling using Bootstrap conventions
- Added Popper.js dependency for Bootstrap functionality
- Added Autoprefixer initialiser for source map support
- Resolved open-ended gem versioning warnings with explicit version minimums for Faraday dependencies
- Updated `faraday-follow_redirects` to 0.4.0
- Updated `lr_common_styles` gem to v3.0.0 (Bootstrap 5)
- Updated `data_services_api` gem to v1.6.1
- Enabled Sass source maps in development for easier front-end debugging
- Added `update` Makefile target to check outdated dependencies
- Streamlined Makefile with inline help documentation
- Cleaned up startup log output formatting
- Removed duplicated `_search-form.scss` partial (consolidated into `_workflow-actions.scss`)

## Breaking Changes

This release updates Bootstrap from 3.x to 5.x via the `lr_common_styles` gem
v3.0.0. Ensure any downstream dependencies or custom styling are compatible
with Bootstrap 5.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/epimorphics/ppd-explorer/compare/v2.2.3...v2.3.0

author: joewoodhouse
body:
## Problem

Android ANR (Application Not Responding) occurs when compass sensor events fire too frequently, causing the main thread to block on WebView bridge operations.

### Stack Trace

```
androidx.webkit.WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported (WebViewFeature.java:747)
com.getcapacitor.MessageHandler.sendResponseMessage (MessageHandler.java:125)
com.getcapacitor.PluginCall.resolve (PluginCall.java:55)
com.getcapacitor.Plugin.notifyListeners (Plugin.java:681)
app.capgo.capacitor.compass.CapgoCompassPlugin.lambda$startListening$0 (CapgoCompassPlugin.java:66)
app.capgo.capacitor.compass.CapgoCompass.onSensorChanged (CapgoCompass.java:134)
android.hardware.SystemSensorManager$SensorEventQueue.dispatchSensorEvent (SystemSensorManager.java:1142)
```

### Root Cause

1. Android sensor events fire 10-20+ times per second with `SENSOR_DELAY_NORMAL`
2. Every sensor event triggers `notifyListeners()` which crosses the WebView bridge
3. WebView operations (`isFeatureSupported`) can be slow and block the main thread
4. When events pile up, the main thread freezes → ANR

## Solution

### Android Changes

- **Background thread processing**: Sensor events now process on a dedicated `HandlerThread` instead of the main thread
- **Time-based throttling**: Configurable minimum interval between events (default: 100ms = max 10 events/sec)
- **Change-based throttling**: Configurable minimum heading change to trigger an event (default: 2°)
- **Main thread posting**: Only posts to UI thread when actually sending an event
- **Removed noisy logging**: Removed `Log.d()` call on every heading calculation

### iOS Changes

- **Built-in heading filter**: Set `locationManager.headingFilter = 1.0` to reduce native event frequency
- **Time-based throttling**: Matching Android behavior (default: 100ms)
- **Change-based throttling**: Matching Android behavior (default: 2°)

### API Changes

Added optional `ListeningOptions` parameter to `startListening()`:

```typescript
interface ListeningOptions {
  /** Minimum interval between events in ms (default: 100) */
  minInterval?: number;
  
  /** Minimum heading change in degrees (default: 2.0) */
  minHeadingChange?: number;
}

// Usage - defaults work for most apps
await CapgoCompass.startListening();

// Custom throttling for high-frequency updates (AR/gaming)
await CapgoCompass.startListening({
  minInterval: 50,
  minHeadingChange: 1.0
});

// Battery-saving mode for navigation
await CapgoCompass.startListening({
  minInterval: 200,
  minHeadingChange: 5.0
});
```

## Breaking Changes

None. The new options are optional with sensible defaults that match or improve upon previous behavior.

## Testing

- [x] Tested on Android device - no ANR observed
- [x] Tested on iOS device - heading updates work correctly
- [x] Verified throttling reduces event frequency as expected
- [x] Verified heading wraparound handling (359° → 1° = 2° change, not 358°)

## Checklist

- [x] Android implementation
- [x] iOS implementation  
- [x] TypeScript definitions updated
- [x] Backward compatible (optional parameters with defaults)
- [x] JSDoc updated with examples

- Added `ConfigUpdate` with TTL and originator tracking
- Added `ResourceSnapshot` for YARN-inspired resource metrics (CPU, memory, disk, load)

**Integration Pattern:**
```cpp
// Setup
GossipConfigManagerConfig config;
config.local_shard_id = "shard-1";
config.gossip_interval_ms = 1000;
config.fanout = 3;

auto manager = std::make_unique<GossipConfigManager>(config, topology, metrics);

// Register callbacks
manager->onConfigUpdate([](const ConfigUpdate& update) {
    // Handle config changes dynamically
});

manager->onResourceSnapshot([](const ResourceSnapshot& snapshot) {
    // Load balancing decisions based on resource state
});

// Publish
manager->publishConfigUpdate("shard.replication_factor", "3");
manager->start();
```

**Vector Clock Conflict Resolution:**
- Ordering determines causality: BEFORE, AFTER, CONCURRENT, EQUAL
- Concurrent updates resolved via last-write-wins (timestamp)
- Metrics track conflict resolution rate

This PR delivers a complete markdown-first jot storage system with SQLite indexing, enabling rapid note capture and retrieval for the Scribel application.

## Key Features

✅ **Markdown-First Storage**
- Jots stored as `.md` files with YAML frontmatter in `.scribel/jots/`
- Obsidian-compatible format

author: rjmsilveira
body:
## What

Fixed a bug in the API controller where `CommentCommand.Name` was not being set when creating commands, causing the command type to default to `Apply` (value `0`) instead of the intended command type (`Plan` or `Apply`).

**Changes:**
- Added `cmdName command.Name` parameter to the `getCommands()` function
- Set `Name: cmdName` on each `CommentCommand` struct created for projects and paths
- Updated `apiPlan()` to pass `command.Plan` to `getCommands()`
- Updated `apiApply()` to pass `command.Apply` to `getCommands()`

## Why

The `command.Name` type is defined using `iota`:

```go
const (
    Apply Name = iota  // = 0
    Plan               // = 1
    // ...
)
```

When the API controller created `CommentCommand` structs, the `Name` field was never set:

```go
cc = append(cc, &events.CommentCommand{
    ProjectName: project,  // Name field missing!
})
```

Since Go initializes unset fields to their zero value, `Name` defaulted to `0`, which is `Apply`. This caused:
- API **plan** requests to have their `CommentCommand.Name` incorrectly set to `Apply`
- The downstream `BuildPlanCommands()` function received the wrong command name via `cmd.CommandName()`
- Pre-workflow hooks and other logic that depends on the command name would behave incorrectly

### How the issue was detected

The bug was discovered when using `pre_workflow_hooks` with the `commands` filter set to `plan`:

```yaml
repos:
  - id: /.*/
    pre_workflow_hooks:
      - run: bash /path/to/script.sh
        description: Running script for plan only
        commands: plan
```

When calling the API `/api/plan` endpoint, the pre-workflow hook was **not executing** even though it should only run for `plan` commands. Investigation revealed that the `CommentCommand.Name` was incorrectly set to `Apply` (the zero value) instead of `Plan`, causing the `commands: plan` filter to skip the hook.

## Tests

Existing tests in `server/controllers/api_controller_test.go` cover this functionality:

- `TestAPIController_Plan` - verifies `BuildPlanCommands` is called correctly
- `TestAPIController_Apply` - verifies `BuildApplyCommands` is called correctly
- Both tests verify the correct number of calls and successful responses

**New tests added** to specifically verify the `CommentCommand.Name` is correctly set for pre-workflow hooks:

- `TestAPIController_Plan_PreWorkflowHooksReceiveCorrectCommand` - verifies that when calling the Plan API endpoint, the pre-workflow hooks receive a `CommentCommand` with `Name` set to `command.Plan`
- `TestAPIController_Apply_PreWorkflowHooksReceiveCorrectCommand` - verifies that when calling the Apply API endpoint, the pre-workflow hooks receive the correct `CommentCommand.Name` for each phase (`command.Plan` for the plan phase, `command.Apply` for the apply phase)

These tests use pegomock's `GetCapturedArguments()` to capture the actual `CommentCommand` passed to `RunPreHooks()` and assert that the `Name` field is correctly set.

To run the tests:
```bash
go test ./server/controllers/... -run "TestAPIController" -v
```

## References

- `command.Name` iota definition: `server/events/command/name.go`
- `CommentCommand` struct: `server/events/comment_command.go`
- `BuildPlanCommands` uses `cmd.CommandName()`: `server/events/project_command_builder.go:279`
- `getCommands()` function: `server/controllers/api_controller.go:59`
- Pre-workflow hooks `commands` filter: `server/events/pre_workflow_hooks_command_runner.go`

author: ihebdhouibi
body:
# Fix: Update deprecated langchain import

## Description

This PR fixes the deprecated langchain import path that causes `ModuleNotFoundError` in the retriever component.

## Problem

The retriever module uses a deprecated import:
```python
from langchain.docstore.document import Document
```

This causes `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langchain.docstore'` as the langchain library has deprecated this import path and moved it to the `langchain_core` package.

**Location**: `paddlex/inference/pipelines/components/retriever/base.py:25`

## Root Cause

The langchain library deprecated the `langchain.docstore.document` import path and moved it to `langchain_core.documents`. This is part of langchain's modularization effort to separate core functionality into dedicated packages.

Reference: [LangChain Documentation](https://python.langchain.com/docs/versions/migrating_chains/conversation_chain/)

## Solution

Updated the import statement to use the new import path from `langchain_core`:
```python
from langchain_core.documents import Document
```

This change ensures compatibility with current and future versions of langchain while maintaining backward compatibility with existing code.

## Changes

- Modified `paddlex/inference/pipelines/components/retriever/base.py`:
  - Line 25: Updated import from `langchain.docstore.document` to `langchain_core.documents`

## Testing

This fix ensures that:
1. The langchain Document class is available through the core module
2. The retriever module functions correctly
3. PP-ChatOCR pipelines with retriever functionality work as expected
4. No breaking changes to existing PaddleX functionality

## Impact

- ✅ Fixes compatibility with modern langchain versions
- ✅ No breaking changes to the PaddleX API
- ✅ Maintains all existing functionality
- ✅ Resolves runtime errors in retriever components

## Related Issues

- Originally identified while working on PaddleOCR
- Submitted to PaddleOCR as PR [#17341](https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR/pull/17341)
- Redirected to PaddleX as this is where the actual dependency issue exists

## Additional Notes

The `langchain_core` package is a required dependency for langchain and is already part of the langchain ecosystem. This change simply updates the import path to use the correct modern location of the `Document` class.

This commit makes substantial updates to the build guide.

My goal was to write a guide that would take a reader from the Shopping List all the way across the finish line. This is quite the undertaking for the reader, so I built in as many "checkpoints" as I could where the reader could validate their work before moving on.

A consequence of my "all the way across the finish line" approach is that the separate software guide ended up getting subsumed into the single build guide. I think this is fair because weaving the software through the physical assembly gives the reader many more opportunities to check their work, e.g. by confirming SSH access on battery power or testing the speaker after soldering it on.

I tried not to make assumptions about the reader's skills or knowledge in technical topics like soldering or command-line interfaces.

# Upgrade from Java 8 to Java 21 with Spring Boot 3.2.2

## Summary

This PR upgrades the Spring Boot RealWorld application from Java 11 to Java 21, along with Spring Boot 2.6.3 to 3.2.2 and all related dependencies. The upgrade follows a milestone-based approach to ensure the system remains buildable throughout.

**Key changes:**
- Java 11 → 21, Gradle 7.4 → 8.5, Spring Boot 2.6.3 → 3.2.2
- Migrated all `javax.validation` and `javax.servlet` imports to `jakarta.*` namespace (required for Spring Boot 3.x)
- Replaced deprecated `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` with `SecurityFilterChain` bean pattern
- Updated `antMatchers()` to `requestMatchers()` for Spring Security 6.x
- Migrated jjwt API from 0.11.x to 0.12.x style (`parserBuilder()` → `parser().verifyWith()`)
- Updated DGS GraphQL exception handler to use async `handleException()` method
- Fixed GraphQL PageInfo type to use generated types instead of `graphql.relay.PageInfo`

All 68 tests pass locally. Lint checks pass.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify security configuration in `WebSecurityConfig.java`** - The migration from `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` to `SecurityFilterChain` is a significant change. Confirm all endpoint authorization rules are correctly preserved (especially `/articles/feed` requiring auth, `/users` and `/users/login` being public)
- [ ] **Test JWT authentication flow end-to-end** - The `DefaultJwtService.java` has API changes for token creation and parsing. Manually test user registration, login, and authenticated requests
- [ ] **Check `.github/workflows/gradle.yml`** - There appears to be a typo (`reat` on line 24) that may cause CI issues
- [ ] **Verify GraphQL pagination** - The `PageInfo` type change in datafetchers should be tested with actual GraphQL queries using `first`/`after` pagination

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Run the application locally with `./gradlew bootRun`
2. Test user registration: `POST /users`
3. Test login: `POST /users/login`
4. Test authenticated endpoint: `GET /articles/feed` with JWT token
5. Test GraphQL query with pagination

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce a premium, provider-driven Now Playing experience that reliably detects and controls Apple Music and Spotify while avoiding misleading fallbacks.
- Keep the existing ambient noise engine unchanged and focus media work on App Store-safe approaches (AppleScript for scripting, no private APIs).

### Description
- Add a `NowPlayingProvider` protocol and concrete providers `AppleMusicProvider` and `SpotifyProvider` that use asynchronous AppleScript via `AppleScriptRunner` to fetch running/playing state, metadata, and artwork and to perform play/pause/next/previous actions.
- Add `NowPlayingRouter` (an `ObservableObject`) that polls providers (~750ms interval), prioritizes Apple Music if playing, falls back to Spotify, and exposes the unified state to SwiftUI: `title`, `artist`, `artwork`, `sourceName`, `isPlaying`, and `isAvailable`.
- Update `MediaControlBar` to bind only to `NowPlayingRouter`, show high-quality artwork and metadata when available, provide responsive `previous` / `playPause` / `next` controls, and display an honest premium empty state `"No supported music playing" / "Start Apple Music or Spotify"` when no supported source is active.
- Add a `QQMusicProvider` placeholder (disabled) with a clear comment that it will be enabled only via an official SDK in future work.
- Integrate the router into the app wiring by adding `nowPlayingRouter` to `AppState` and propagating it through the UI; remove previous generic music-panel/menu paths and the MusicController system-media coupling so the app does not pretend to support unsupported sources.
- Implementations include safe, asynchronous AppleScript execution, Spotify artwork URL caching and remote fetch, and non-blocking polling on a background task.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run as part of this change.

body: ### Description Just small changes in order to run integration testing framework work again. Besides removed the shadow mode [here](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/8727/files#diff-faff1af3d8ff408964a57b2e475f69a6b7c7b71c9978cccc8f471798caac2c88R207), so after this PR specs CI will fail if something happens with these harness integration tests. Besides, note that I removed almost all previous specs files, since those were not super useful, and we should start simple instead, so in favor of that I am leaving just `tests/specs/grpc_recorded_session_single_root.json`, which essentially: 1. Logs in within cline provider `accountLoginClicked` 2. Gets user organizations `getUserOrganizations` 3. Creates a new task `newTask` 4. Get's state to verify internal status `getLatestState` This PR makes minimal changes to get the integration testing framework running again. I've removed shadow mode here, so after this lands the specs CI will fail if the integration test harness detects regressions. This is intentional, so failures are surfaced instead of silently ignored. I also removed most of the existing spec files. They weren’t providing much signal, and I want to restart with a simpler, more focused baseline. For now, I’m keeping a single spec `tests/specs/grpc_recorded_session_single_root.json`. This spec covers a minimal but representative flow: 1. Log in via the cline provider (`accountLoginClicked`) 2. Fetch user organizations (`getUserOrganizations`) 3. Create a new task (`newTask`) 4. Fetch state to validate internal status (`getLatestState`) The goal here is to lock in a small, high-signal scenario first, and expand coverage incrementally once we’re confident the framework is adding value. Note that we validate things under response and gathering the latest state, and note that we can partially validate the latest state setting up the metadata, so is flexible enough to verify everything we might want. E.g: ``` .... "meta": { "synthetic": true, "expected": { "stateJson":{ "taskHistory": [ { "task":"Something wrong?" } ] } } }, ... ``` ### Test Procedure Running tests is as easy as running this: ```npm run test:tp-orchestrator -- tests/specs/ --count=1``` You can run the same orchestrator enabling logs to gather more information ```npm run test:tp-orchestrator -- tests/specs/ --count=1 --server-logs``` Besides, you can debug everything by running the standalone in debug mode in VS, +setting up breakpoints within the standalone and debug everything real quick without doing any guess: ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots Ran the only spec file with `count=10` to triple check flakiness: ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fix integration testing framework by removing outdated tests, ensuring CI fails on test failures, and simplifying to a single spec file. > > - **Integration Testing Framework**: > - Removed shadow mode in `test.yml` to ensure CI fails on integration test failures. > - Deleted most spec files, retaining only `grpc_recorded_session_single_root.json` for a minimal test flow. > - **Scripts**: > - Modified `test-standalone-core-api-server.ts` to overwrite existing files when extracting `standalone.zip`. > - **Spec File**: > - Updated `grpc_recorded_session_single_root.json` to include expected response values and metadata. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 903b646d1fd1bee329e222f0daf8cad19a346414. author: copilot
body:
All API requests were attempting full server rotation on every call, causing resource waste. This PR fixes the issue by implementing a clean, unified approach where all requests use the same sequential retry logic.

## Changes

### Unified server rotation
- All API requests now use `tryWithRotation` directly for consistent behavior
- Servers are tried sequentially from top to bottom on every request
- On any error, the next server in the list is attempted
- No optimization, no session tracking - simple and predictable

### Updated API clients
- `kvServerProvider.js`: All methods (loadData, saveData, loadKeys, loadNamespaceInfo, updateNamespaceInfo) → `tryWithRotation`
- `api.js`: getNamespaceInfo → `tryWithRotation`
- Connection testing: Uses `tryWithRotation` (unchanged)

### Implementation
```javascript
// All requests use the same unified approach
const data = await tryWithRotation(async (serverUrl) => {
  return await axios.get(`${serverUrl}/kv/${key}`);
});
// Always tries servers in order: server 1, server 2, etc.
// No distinction between primary and other servers
```

## Benefits
- ✅ **Simple and predictable** - Same behavior for all requests
- ✅ **No duplicate requests** - Each server tried only once per request
- ✅ **Easy to understand** - No complex optimization logic
- ✅ **Unified codebase** - Single pattern across all API methods
- ✅ **Resource efficient** - Tries servers sequentially, stops on first success

## Kconfig: Add ALLOW_CUSTOM_PERMISSIVE_COMPONENTS license option

### Summary

This PR adds a new license configuration option `ALLOW_CUSTOM_PERMISSIVE_COMPONENTS` for components that have custom permissive licenses which are not covered by the standard license options. This addresses the need identified in nuttx-apps#3343 for handling components like the Whetstone benchmark which have custom permissive license terms.

### Changes

#### Files Modified

1. **Kconfig**
   - Added new `ALLOW_CUSTOM_PERMISSIVE_COMPONENTS` config option under "License Setup" menu
   - Follows the existing pattern of other license options (BSD, GPL, MIT, etc.)

2. **Documentation/quickstart/configuring.rst**
   - Added documentation for the new License Setup section
   - Lists all available `ALLOW_*_COMPONENTS` options with descriptions

### Technical Details

**New License Option:**
- Enables projects to explicitly opt-in to using components with custom permissive licenses
- Covers licenses that allow free use, modification, and distribution
- Covers licenses with specific attribution or notice requirements
- Does not cover restrictive/proprietary licenses

**Integration:**
- Placed after `ALLOW_ICS_COMPONENTS` in the License Setup menu
- Default value is `n` (disabled) for safety
- Components with custom permissive licenses should add `depends on ALLOW_CUSTOM_PERMISSIVE_COMPONENTS`

### Impact

- **License Compliance**: Provides explicit opt-in mechanism for custom permissive licensed code
- **User Awareness**: Forces users to acknowledge custom license requirements
- **Consistency**: Follows established NuttX license configuration patterns

### Usage

Enable option with:
CONFIG_ALLOW_CUSTOM_PERMISSIVE_COMPONENTS=y

### Testing

Configuration option verified.

### Reference

which discussed in https://github.com/apache/nuttx-apps/pull/3343

author: copilot
body:
Window appears but remains unresponsive with spinning cursor because `AppState` initialization synchronously queries MediaPlayer framework during SwiftUI's first render cycle.

## Root Cause

```swift
@StateObject private var appState = AppState()  // Triggers init during render

init() {
    // ...
    systemMedia.connect()  // ← Blocks main thread querying MPNowPlayingInfoCenter
}
```

## Changes

**Defer MediaPlayer queries until after first render:**
- Removed `systemMedia.connect()` from `AppState.init()`
- Removed immediate `refreshNowPlayingInfo()` from `SystemMediaController.startObserving()`
- Added `.task` modifier to `MainWindowView` that calls `connect()` post-render

**DEBUG diagnostics (compile-time gated):**
- Console logs tracking init → render → service connection sequence
- UI indicators showing boot completion and service status
- Stripped entirely in Release builds via `#if DEBUG`

## Result

UI becomes interactive immediately. MediaPlayer connection happens asynchronously after window appears. All functionality preserved.

```swift
// MainWindowView.swift
.task {
    // Connect to system media after first render to prevent blocking main thread
    appState.systemMedia.connect()
}
```

body: Aligns video frame extraction with `ffmpeg -vf fps` filter behavior to ensure equivalent frame sampling and selection logic. The previous logic could diverge from `ffmpeg`'s `fps` filter due to floating-point precision, seek behavior, and tie-breaking rules. This update uses integer microsecond timestamps, a global FPS grid, and `AV_ROUND_NEAR_INF` for tie-breaking, closely mimicking `ffmpeg`'s `fps` filter with `round=near` and `eof_action=round`. ---

author: dancho07
body:
### Motivation
- Provide an editable, persistent watchlist and per-row favorites on the Market Pulse page so users can manage symbols without editing source code. 
- Keep all existing filters, sorting and refresh behaviour intact while ensuring newly added/removed symbols are respected by the refresh loop. 

### Description
- Replaced the previous hardcoded watchlist with a `DEFAULT_WATCHLIST` and a new storage-backed layer implemented via a `createStorageAdapter(storage)` adapter and stores: `createWatchlistStore(...)` (key `watchlist_v1`) and `createFavoritesStore(...)` (key `favorites_v1`).
- Exposed watchlist API functions and behavior through the store: `getWatchlist()`, `addSymbol()`, `removeSymbol()`, and `resetToDefault()`; symbols are normalized (trim + `toUpperCase`) and validated (A–Z, 0–9, `.` or `-`, 1–10 chars), and persisted via `storage.set`/`storage.get`.
- Added UI controls to `live.html` and `styles.css`: an `Add symbol` input/button, inline watchlist error display (`watchlist-error`), and a `Show favorites only` toggle; table columns now include favorite and remove cells.
- Row actions: star toggle for favorites (updates `favorites_v1`) and a remove button that deletes a symbol from the watchlist and removes it from favorites; Analyze still navigates to `index.html?symbol=XYZ&autorun=1` (updated to use `window.location.href`).
- Integrated favorites into the existing filter pipeline by implementing `getMarketFilterValues()`, `matchesFilters(...)`, and `applyMarketFilters(...)` so the pipeline is: data -> (favorites filter if enabled) -> existing filters -> sort -> render.
- Synced market state with the watchlist via `syncMarketStateWithWatchlist()` and guarded refresh logic so removed symbols are ignored immediately (`isSymbolInWatchlist()` checks in `refreshSymbolData`, `refreshVisibleQuotes`, and historical fetch paths) to avoid requesting removed symbols and to safely ignore in-flight results.
- Added helper `removeSymbolFromWatchlist(...)` to centralize removal + favorites cleanup and kept a single `storageAdapter` layer to make future sync/back-end swapping straightforward.

### Testing
- Added tests to `tests/app.test.js` covering: load default watchlist when storage empty, `addSymbol` normalization and validation, `removeSymbol` updates watchlist + favorites, favorites-only filter respecting sector/cap/signal filters, and persistence across reloads using a mocked storage adapter. 
- Ran the full test suite with `node tests/app.test.js`; automated tests passed (all tests reported as ✓).

- add a failing test exposing a cjs/esm compatibility issue in compartment-mapper
- fix missing inference from package.json->exports `import` field

The way it fixes the test is not exactly matching what node.js would do in the same situation.
Node.js loads the file in `package.json->exports['./sha2'].require` but Endo loads the one from `package.json->exports['./sha2'].import`.
All this fix is doing is correcting the module type inference for `package.json->exports` in general.

Changing the behavior of selecting import vs require could happen elsewhere, but it seems unimportant in Endo (until we find a package that ships breaking changes in one version across esm and cjs variants)

author: copilot
body:
Moved `defaultValue` computation from server-side to client-side across all input types. Each input type now implements `createDefaultValue()` to parse and validate default values according to its value type.

## Changes by input type

- **Checkbox**: Parses `'checked'` string to boolean
- **ComboBox, NoInputTypeFoundView, TextInputType**: Validates string input, returns null for non-strings
- **NumberInputType (Double, Long)**: Validates numeric input, returns null for non-numbers
- **Date, Time**: Pattern-matches ISO format; falls back to `RelativeTimeParser` for expressions like `+1d`, `-2h`, `now`
- **DateTimeRange, PrincipalSelector**: Returns null (no default values supported)

## Supporting changes

- **RelativeTimeParser**: Added `parseToDate()` and `parseToTime()` methods to support date/time-specific relative expressions
- **DateHelper.isoValueToDate()**: Added `mode` parameter to support date-only and time-only ISO formatting
- **DateTime, Instant**: Removed server-side default value injection logic

Example usage:
```typescript
// Date input with relative time expression
createDefaultValue('+7d')  // Returns value 7 days from now

// Number input with validation
createDefaultValue(42)     // Returns numeric value
createDefaultValue('foo')  // Returns null value
```

author: copilot
body:
Slack's `chat.postMessage` API requires specific formatting for clickable mentions: `<@USERID>` for users or `<!subteam^GROUPID>` for user groups. Plain text like `@username` or `<@username>` (with handle instead of ID) renders as plain text.

## Changes

- **RELEASE.yaml**: Replace `@connectors-release-manager` with `${{ secrets.CONNECTORS_RELEASE_MANAGER_SLACK_GROUP_ID }}`
- **DEPLOY_SNAPSHOTS.yaml**: Replace `@connector-medic` with `${{ secrets.CONNECTORS_MEDIC_SLACK_GROUP_ID }}`
- **SLACK_MENTIONS_SETUP.md**: Document secret configuration and ID lookup methods

Example change:
```yaml
"text": ":alarm: ${{ secrets.CONNECTORS_RELEASE_MANAGER_SLACK_GROUP_ID }} Release workflow failed..."
```

## Required Setup

Configure these secrets with proper Slack mention format:
- `CONNECTORS_RELEASE_MANAGER_SLACK_GROUP_ID` 
- `CONNECTORS_MEDIC_SLACK_GROUP_ID`

Format depends on target type:
- User: `<@U024BE7LH>` (get from Slack profile → Copy member ID)
- User group: `<!subteam^S0123456789>` (get from `usergroups.list` API)

See `.github/workflows/SLACK_MENTIONS_SETUP.md` for details.

body:
💡 **What:**
- Implemented a unified "Soft Confirm" UX pattern for all delete actions in the admin interface (Templates, Schedules, Voices, Structures, Sections).
- Replaced intrusive browser `confirm()` alerts with a smoother in-place confirmation (button text changes to "Click again to confirm" for 3 seconds).
- Added visual feedback (red color) for the confirmation state.
- Localized the confirmation string.

🎯 **Why:**
- To improve user experience by making destructive actions smoother and less jarring.
- To maintain context during confirmation (user doesn't have to look away or dismiss a modal).
- To consistency across the application's admin interface.

📸 **Visual Changes:**
- Delete buttons now turn red and change text to "Click again to confirm" when clicked once, reverting after 3 seconds if not confirmed.

♿ **Accessibility:**
- The pattern maintains keyboard focus on the button.
- The visual change (color) is accompanied by text change, ensuring accessibility for colorblind users.

### Update [asgiref](https://pypi.org/project/asgiref) from **3.2.5** to **3.11.0**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.11.0
   ```
   -------------------

* ``sync_to_async`` gains a ``context`` parameter, similar to those for
  ``asyncio.create_task``, ``TaskGroup`` &co, that can be used on Python 3.11+ to
  control the context used by the underlying task.

  The parent context is already propagated by default but the additional
  control is useful if multiple ``sync_to_async`` calls need to share the same
  context, e.g. when used with ``asyncio.gather()``.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.10.0
   ```
   -------------------

* Added AsyncSingleThreadContext context manager to ensure multiple AsyncToSync
  invocations use the same thread. (511)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.9.2
   ```
   ------------------

* Adds support for Python 3.14.

* Fixes wsgi.errors file descriptor in WsgiToAsgi adapter.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.9.1
   ```
   ------------------

* Fixed deletion of Local values affecting other contexts. (523)

* Skip CPython specific garbage collection test on pypy. (521)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.9.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Adds support for Python 3.13.

* Drops support for (end-of-life) Python 3.8.

* Fixes an error with conflicting kwargs between AsyncToSync and the wrapped
  function. (471)

* Fixes Local isolation between asyncio Tasks. (478)

* Fixes a reference cycle in Local (508)

* Fixes a deadlock in CurrentThreadExecutor with nested async_to_sync →
  sync_to_async → async_to_sync → create_task calls. (494)

* The ApplicationCommunicator testing utility will now return the task result
  if it's already completed on send_input and receive_nothing. You may need to
  catch (e.g.) the asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError if sending messages to
  already finished consumers in your tests. (505)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.8.1
   ```
   ------------------

* Fixes a regression in 3.8.0 affecting nested task cancellation inside
  sync_to_async.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.8.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Adds support for Python 3.12.

* Drops support for (end-of-life) Python 3.7.

* Fixes task cancellation propagation to subtasks when using synchronous Django
  middleware.

* Allows nesting ``sync_to_async`` via ``asyncio.wait_for``.

* Corrects WSGI adapter handling of root path.

* Handles case where `"client"` is ``None`` in WsgiToAsgi adapter.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.7.2
   ```
   ------------------

* The type annotations for SyncToAsync and AsyncToSync have been changed to
  more accurately reflect the kind of callables they return.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.7.1
   ```
   ------------------

* On Python 3.10 and below, the version of the "typing_extensions" package
  is now constrained to be at least version 4 (as we depend on functionality
  in that version and above)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.7.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Contextvars are now required for the implementation of `sync` as Python 3.6
  is now no longer a supported version.

* sync_to_async and async_to_sync now pass-through

* Debug and Lifespan State extensions have resulted in a typing change for some
  request and response types. This change should be backwards-compatible.

* ``asgiref`` frames will now be hidden in Django tracebacks by default.

* Raw performance and garbage collection improvements in Local, SyncToAsync,
  and AsyncToSync.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.6.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Two new functions are added to the ``asgiref.sync`` module: ``iscoroutinefunction()``
  and ``markcoroutinefunction()``.

  Python 3.12 deprecates ``asyncio.iscoroutinefunction()`` as an alias for
  ``inspect.iscoroutinefunction()``, whilst also removing the ``_is_coroutine`` marker.
  The latter is replaced with the ``inspect.markcoroutinefunction`` decorator.

  The new ``asgiref.sync`` functions are compatibility shims for these
  functions that can be used until Python 3.12 is the minimum supported
  version.

  **Note** that these functions are considered **beta**, and as such, whilst
  not likely, are subject to change in a point release, until the final release
  of Python 3.12. They are included in ``asgiref`` now so that they can be
  adopted by Django 4.2, in preparation for support of Python 3.12.

* The ``loop`` argument to ``asgiref.timeout.timeout`` is deprecated. As per other
  ``asyncio`` based APIs, the running event loop is used by default. Note that
  ``asyncio`` provides timeout utilities from Python 3.11, and these should be
  preferred where available.

* Support for the ``ASGI_THREADS`` environment variable, used by
  ``SyncToAsync``, is removed. In general, a running event-loop is not
  available to `asgiref` at import time, and so the default thread pool
  executor cannot be configured. Protocol servers, or applications, should set
  the default executor as required when configuring the event loop at
  application startup.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.5.2
   ```
   ------------------

* Allow async-callables class instances to be passed to AsyncToSync
  without warning

* Prevent giving async-callable class instances to SyncToAsync
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.5.1
   ```
   ------------------

* sync_to_async in thread-sensitive mode now works corectly when the
  outermost thread is synchronous (214)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.5.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Python 3.6 is no longer supported, and asyncio calls have been changed to
  use only the modern versions of the APIs as a result

* Several causes of RuntimeErrors in cases where an event loop was assigned
  to a thread but not running

* Speed improvements in the Local class
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.4.1
   ```
   ------------------

* Fixed an issue with the deadlock detection where it had false positives
  during exception handling.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.4.0
   ```
   ------------------

* Calling sync_to_async directly from inside itself (which causes a deadlock
  when in the default, thread-sensitive mode) now has deadlock detection.

* asyncio usage has been updated to use the new versions of get_event_loop,
  ensure_future, wait and gather, avoiding deprecation warnings in Python 3.10.
  Python 3.6 installs continue to use the old versions; this is only for 3.7+

* sync_to_async and async_to_sync now have improved type hints that pass
  through the underlying function type correctly.

* All Websocket* types are now spelled WebSocket, to match our specs and the
  official spelling. The old names will work until release 3.5.0, but will
  raise deprecation warnings.

* The typing for WebSocketScope and HTTPScope's `extensions` key has been
  fixed.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.4
   ```
   ------------------

* The async_to_sync type error is now a warning due the high false negative
  rate when trying to detect coroutine-returning callables in Python.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.3
   ```
   ------------------

* The sync conversion functions now correctly detect functools.partial and other
  wrappers around async functions on earlier Python releases.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.2
   ```
   ------------------

* SyncToAsync now takes an optional "executor" argument if you want to supply
  your own executor rather than using the built-in one.

* async_to_sync and sync_to_async now check their arguments are functions of
  the correct type.

* Raising CancelledError inside a SyncToAsync function no longer stops a future

author: anneschuth
body:
## Summary
- Upgrade uvicorn from 0.35.0 to 0.40.0
- Make `nest_asyncio.apply()` lazy to avoid conflicts with uvicorn's new `loop_factory` usage

## Problem
Uvicorn 0.40.0 uses `loop_factory` argument in `asyncio.run()`, but `nest_asyncio` patches `asyncio.run()` without supporting this argument. When `nest_asyncio.apply()` is called at module import time (during server startup), it breaks uvicorn.

## Solution
Delay the `nest_asyncio.apply()` call until the importer websocket is actually used. This allows uvicorn to start normally, and nest_asyncio only gets applied when the LangGraph workflow needs it.

## Test plan
- [x] Server starts locally with uvicorn 0.40.0
- [x] Server responds to requests
- [ ] CI tests pass
- [ ] Importer websocket functionality still works

author: sergeykad
body:
Gradle's task decoration cannot resolve generic type parameters for                                                                                                                                                      
  @Nested properties. When IntelliJ's Gradle tooling API introspects                                                                                                                                                       
  tasks, it triggers getMetaClass() on the decorated task class, which                                                                                                                                                     
  fails with "Cannot invoke Type.getClass() because formal is null".                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  The fix:                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - Change @Nested to @Internal on the generic configuration property                                                                                                                                                      
    in Js2dGeneratorTaskBase                                                                                                                                                                                               
  - Add a separate nestedConfiguration property with @Nested and the                                                                                                                                                       
    concrete type Js2pConfiguration in Js2pGenerationTask                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  This preserves Gradle's input tracking for the nested configuration                                                                                                                                                      
  while avoiding the reflection issue with generic type parameters.                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  Fixes compatibility with Gradle 9.x and IntelliJ IDEA 2025.x.
See https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/properties_providers.html

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
⚡ Bolt: Optimized Lambert Solver Memory & Speed

💡 **What:**
- Replaced the memory-intensive `np.sum(r1*r2, axis=-1)` dot product with `np.einsum('...k, ...k -> ...', r1, r2)`.
- Pre-allocated the `diff` buffer outside the Secant loop to avoid creating a new array in every iteration.
- Implemented buffer reuse in `_compute_t_internal` to repurpose `term` and `rat_v` arrays for subsequent calculations.

🎯 **Why:**
- **Memory Bottleneck:** The original dot product calculation broadcasted two input arrays (e.g., `(1, N, 3)` and `(M, 1, 3)`) into a massive `(M, N, 3)` array before summing. For a 2000x2000 grid, this allocated ~96MB unnecessarily. `einsum` computes the sum-product on the fly.
- **Allocation Overhead:** Python/NumPy allocation overhead accumulates in tight loops. Pre-allocating `diff` removes this cost from the hot path.

📊 **Impact:**
- **Dot Product Speedup:** ~5.4x faster (benchmark verified).
- **Overall Solver Speedup:** ~8% faster for typical grid sizes.
- **Memory Reduction:** Eliminated the largest temporary array allocation in the solver.

🔬 **Measurement:**
- Verified with `benchmark_dot.py` showing `np.einsum` taking 0.035s vs `np.sum` taking 0.193s for 2000x2000 grid.
- Verified with `benchmark_lambert.py` showing execution time drop from 0.45s to 0.42s for 250k points.
- Passed all unit tests, including regression check for integer inputs.

---

author: spbanzay
body:
### Motivation
- Live chat experienced inconsistent ordering and parsing because WebSocket live messages used DB timestamp format while API messages were returned as RFC3339, causing the frontend to mix differently-formatted timestamps and break pagination/ordering. 
- The messages endpoint returned messages in a different iteration order than the frontend expected, which led to duplicated reversing logic and incorrect page boundaries.

### Description
- Normalize timestamps emitted over WebSocket by converting the DB `created_at` string (e.g. `2006-01-02 15:04:05`) to RFC3339 before sending in `ServeWS` (`internal/handlers/ws.go`).
- Preserve the database batch order when building the `/api/messages` response by iterating `msgs` in returned order instead of reversing it, so the handler aligns with `GetMessagesBetween` (which returns DESC) and frontend pagination (`internal/handlers/handlers.go`).
- Small refactor keeps `created_at` consistent between API and WS payloads to avoid client-side parsing/ordering discrepancies.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run as part of this change (no `go test` executed).

body:
This pull request introduces a major upgrade to the Chart of Accounts (CoA) system, expanding support for professional accounting features such as inventory, fixed assets, VAT, and payroll. It adds a comprehensive new CoA template, updates the database schema to support contra accounts, and provides a migration script to upgrade existing tenants. Additionally, it refines journal entry logic to use new standardized account codes for greater consistency and best practices.

**Chart of Accounts Expansion and Schema Updates:**

- Enhanced the `FAMILY_COA_TEMPLATE` in `accountingService.js` to a professional-grade CoA, adding many new accounts (inventory, VAT, payroll, contra accounts, etc.), standardized numbering, and an `isContra` flag for contra accounts.
- Updated the `Account` model in `schema.prisma` to include a new `isContra` boolean field, supporting identification of contra accounts in the database.

**Migration and Upgrade Script:**

- Added `scripts/upgradeCoA.js`, a migration script that upgrades all existing tenants to the new CoA template. It creates missing accounts, updates the `isContra` field where needed, and provides a summary report after execution.

**Accounting Logic Improvements (Inventory & Fixed Assets):**

- Updated inventory adjustment journal logic to use new standardized account codes (e.g., 1300 for Inventory Asset, 5200 for COGS) and clarified comments for better maintainability. author: copilot
body:
Social media icons (Snapchat, TikTok, SoundCloud) had truncated SVG paths causing rendering issues. The service worker used stale-while-revalidate caching, preventing users from receiving timely updates.

## Changes

**Icon Rendering** (`index.html`, `styles.css`)
- Replaced truncated SVG paths with complete path data for all three social icons
- Increased icon size from 48px to 64px for high-DPI displays
- Added `shape-rendering: geometricPrecision` for improved SVG clarity

**Caching Strategy** (`service-worker.js`)
- Changed from stale-while-revalidate to network-first for static assets
- Bumped cache version from v2 to v3
- Enhanced error handling with resource-specific logging and graceful fallback

```javascript
// Before: stale-while-revalidate (returns cache immediately)
event.respondWith(
    caches.match(request).then(cached => cached || fetchPromise)
);

// After: network-first (tries network, falls back to cache)
event.respondWith(
    fetch(request)
        .then(response => {
            cache.put(request, response.clone());
            return response;
        })
        .catch(() => caches.match(request))
);
```

## Screenshots

**Social media icons now render at 64px with complete SVG paths:**

![Social Icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf6f32d2-8a77-4e83-9a01-df34ad2835bd)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Resolve issues with the social media icons in the "index.html" file and improve the caching strategy as follows:

> 1. Replace truncated SVG paths for the social media icons (Snapchat, TikTok, SoundCloud) with complete SVG paths to ensure proper rendering.

> 3. Use `shape-rendering: geometricPrecision` and `image-rendering: crisp-edges` in the CSS for improved rendering quality.
> 
> ### Caching Strategy Updates:
> 1. Switch the current service worker caching strategy:
>    - Change from `cache-first` to `network-first` strategy for static assets. This ensures updates are fetched from the network when online, improving app freshness.
>    - Implement error handling in case of cache fetch failures.
> 
> 2. Update cache versioning from v2 to v3 to reflect changes in caching settings.
> 
> 3. Add `skipWaiting()` and `clients.claim()` in the service worker to ensure immediate activation of updated service workers.
> 
> ### Testing:
> 1. Validate that the social media icons now render properly and are displayed at the new size on regular and high-resolution displays.
> 2. Ensure that updated files are fetched correctly during subsequent app loads.
> 3. Confirm that the app fallback behavior works correctly when offline (using the cache properly).

author: attila-torp
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent disabling Gutenberg's `form_node_form_alter` globally which hid the Gutenberg editor for nodes that actually have the field. 
- Ensure base field registration for the Gutenberg field type only happens when the `gutenberg` field type plugin is available. 
- Avoid invoking or removing Gutenberg form alter when the configured Gutenberg field is not present on the current node/type. 

### Description
- Add a plugin type check in `labl_blocks_entity_base_field_info()` by loading the `plugin.manager.field.field_type` service and returning early unless `hasDefinition('gutenberg')` is true. 
- Add `labl_blocks_module_implements_alter()` to conditionally remove the `gutenberg` implementation from the `form_node_form_alter` hook list only when `labl_blocks_should_run_gutenberg_form_alter()` returns false. 
- Add `labl_blocks_should_run_gutenberg_form_alter()` which verifies `gutenberg` is enabled, reads the configured field name from `gutenberg.settings`, inspects the current route for a `node` or `node_type`, and returns whether the node (or a created node of that type) `hasField($field_name)`. 
- Keep the decision local to the current node/type so Gutenberg's form alter runs for routes where the field exists and is skipped only when the configured field is absent. 

### Testing

author: elfantasma
body:
**Motivation**

  Per the discv5 spec, implementations should limit `WHOAREYOU` packets per source IP to prevent
  amplification attacks. An attacker can spoof the source IP of a victim, send many small
  packets to our node, and we respond with larger `WHOAREYOU` packets to the victim's
  IP—amplifying the attacker's traffic.

  **Description**

  - Adds a `whoareyou_rate_limit` map to track last `WHOAREYOU` send time per source IP
  - Rate limits `WHOAREYOU` responses to 1 per second per IP address
  - Stale rate limit entries are automatically cleaned up during periodic maintenance
  - Adds unit test `test_whoareyou_rate_limiting` to verify the behavior

  Closes #5849

author: copilot
body:
Multiple users syncing to their devices simultaneously (A→B, C→D, E→F) could lose WebRTC signaling messages due to missing concurrency control in `queueSignal()`. While chunk uploads had retry logic, signal queueing used a simple read-modify-write pattern vulnerable to last-write-wins races.

### Changes

**sessionManager.js**
- Added optimistic concurrency control to `queueSignal()` matching the existing `pushChunk()` pattern
- Unique message IDs for reliable tracking through retries
- Version-based conflict detection with exponential backoff (50ms → 500ms, 5 retries max)

```javascript
// Each signal now tracked by unique ID to prevent false-positive verification
const messageId = `${from}-${type}-${now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;

// Retry loop with version checking
for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_PUSH_RETRIES; attempt++) {
  // ... read, modify, write, verify by messageId, backoff on conflict
}
```

**test/comprehensive-test.js**
- `testMultiUserConcurrentSync()` - 5 user pairs syncing simultaneously
- `testCrossDeviceSync()` - same user syncing A→B, A→C, B→D concurrently  
- `testConcurrentSignalQueueing()` - 10 ICE candidates queued in parallel
- `testMixedConcurrentOperations()` - chunks + signals interleaved

Session isolation via SHA-256 keyed on `(inviteCode, passwordHash)` ensures independent sync sessions never interfere.

author: mowillia
body:
## Summary

Modified the claim reference validation workflow and claim categorization workflow to only process and flag central claims. This change ensures that non-central claims are neither validated nor flagged as issues in the UI, reducing processing time and focusing validation efforts on the most important claims that are central to the document's argument.

## Motivation

Previously, the system validated all claims that needed substantiation, regardless of their centrality to the document's argument. This resulted in:
- Unnecessary processing time and API costs for validating peripheral claims
- UI clutter with issues for non-central claims that don't significantly impact the document's core argument
- Inconsistent behavior where non-central claims were validated but shouldn't be flagged

By filtering to only central claims, we can:
- Reduce processing time and API costs
- Focus validation efforts on claims that matter most to the document's argument
- Ensure consistency between validation behavior and UI issue reporting
- Align with the approach already used in the live reports workflow

## What's Changed

### Backend

- **`lib/workflows/claim_reference_validation/nodes/verify_claims.py`**
  - Added centrality filter in `_verify_chunk_claims_with_provider` function (lines 83-88)
  - Added check to skip non-central claims before verification: `if hasattr(claim, "central") and not claim.central: continue`
  - Added debug logging when claims are skipped due to non-centrality
  - Filter is applied early in the claim iteration loop, before the substantiation check

- **`lib/workflows/claim_extraction/nodes/categorize_claims.py`**
  - Modified `_categorize_single_claim` to apply centrality-based override (lines 128-137)
  - Added check to set `needs_external_verification=False` for non-central claims
  - Updated rationale field to indicate when override is applied: `"[Claim is not central, so external verification not required.]"`
  - Added debug logging when `needs_external_verification` is overridden due to non-centrality
  - Ensures non-central claims won't appear as issues in the UI even if the categorization agent determines they would otherwise need external verification

### Frontend

No frontend changes required. The changes are transparent to the API and don't affect the response structure. The UI will simply show fewer issues for non-central claims.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Risk**: Claims without the `central` attribute might be incorrectly filtered or processed.

**Mitigation**: Both implementations use `hasattr(claim, "central")` to check for the attribute's existence before filtering. Claims without the attribute will be processed as before, ensuring backward compatibility.

**Risk**: Users might expect all claims to be validated, not just central ones.

**Mitigation**: This aligns with the existing behavior in the live reports workflow, which already filters by centrality. The change focuses validation on the most important claims, which is the intended behavior for claim reference validation. Non-central claims are still extracted and categorized, they just don't require validation.

**Risk**: Debug logging might be too verbose in production.

**Mitigation**: The logging uses `logger.debug()`, which only appears when debug logging is enabled, preventing log spam in normal operation.

**Risk**: Rationale field might lose important categorization information when overridden.

**Mitigation**: The rationale is updated to clearly indicate the override reason, though the original categorization reasoning is replaced. If preserving the original rationale is important, this could be enhanced in a future change to append rather than replace.

author: sigilioso
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a refactored version of `sub_agent.rs` in a new temporary module `sub_agent_new.rs`. The refactoring adopts the new `Supervisor` trait that unifies `SupervisorStopper` functionality and adds support delegating to an existing supervisor the application of new configuration via the `apply()` method.

## Changes

### Supervisor apply() usage

**Previous behavior:**
- When a new remote config arrived, the old supervisor was **always stopped** and a new one was **always started**
- This means long interruptions of the agents while installing new agent on 'on-host' environments.

**New behavior:**
- When a new remote config arrives and a supervisor is already running, the system attempts to **apply the configuration without restarting** using `Supervisor::apply()`
  - If there's no existing supervisor does the system fall back to the old "stop and start" approach
  - If `apply()` fails, the `RemoteConfig` is reported as failed and no supervisor keeps running (agents stop).
- This enables **zero-downtime** updates if implemented in the supervisor.

### Supervisor Lifecycle

**Previous behavior:**
```rust
// Old: Explicit stop before starting new supervisor
stop_supervisor(old_supervisor);
new_supervisor.start(...)
```

**New behavior:**
```rust
// New: Try to apply first, only rebuild if necessary
if let Some(existing) = old_supervisor {
    existing.apply(new_config) // Hot-reload attempt
} else {
    build_and_start_new_supervisor()
}
```

‼️ The `Supervisor::apply()` method is responsible for handling any necessary internal restarts.

### Small refactors and improvements

- Simplify error handling: `SupervisorCreationError` is kept on `init_supervisor` only.
- Add new helpers for improving maintainability
- Unit tests are extended to check the configuration updates behaviors when there was a previous supervisor ("aply") and there was no supervisor ("build + start").
- Extend helpers documentation.

## Notes for reviewers

- Because the new behavior is introduced in a different module, this PR is best reviewed **commit-by-commit**.

- The new module is **not yet used** and will replace `sub_agent.rs` once other dependent changes are ready.
  * Adapting the k8s supervisor #2055
  * Adapting the on-hots supervisor

  When the supervisors are ready we need to:

  1. Replace `sub_agent.rs` with `sub_agent_new.rs`
  2. Fix the imports
  3. Replace the supervisors as well

body:
## Summary
- Change Linux builds from `ubuntu-latest` to `ubuntu-22.04` for glibc compatibility

## Problem
Users on Debian 12 cannot run the application:
```
swan-vault-recovery-assistant: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
swan-vault-recovery-assistant: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.39' not found
```

## Root Cause
- `ubuntu-latest` now points to Ubuntu 24.04 with glibc 2.39
- Debian 12 (Bookworm) ships with glibc 2.36
- Binary is dynamically linked against the build system's newer glibc

## Solution
Use `ubuntu-22.04` (glibc 2.35) for Linux builds, ensuring compatibility with Debian 12 and other older distributions.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge and release
- [ ] Verify .deb package works on Debian 12

Fixes PSEC-3675

# Pull Request

## Summary

- Add `since_date` input parameter to filter receipts by creation timestamp
- Enable efficient re-evaluation of newly added receipts without reprocessing the entire dataset
- Filter is applied BEFORE limit sampling, allowing date-bounded random samples

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that resolves an issue)

- [x] No new warnings or linting issues introduced
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines

## Related Issues

None

## Impact Analysis

This is a non-breaking, additive change:
- If `since_date` is not provided (default), behavior is unchanged
- The new parameter flows through: SetDefaults → Initialize → ListAllReceipts Lambda
- Filtering happens in-memory after the DynamoDB scan, so no index changes needed
- Receipts with `timestamp=None` are excluded when `since_date` is specified (safe default)

## Deployment Notes

1. Deploy Pulumi stack to update Step Function definition:
   ```bash
   cd infra && pulumi up --stack dev
   ```

   ```bash
   aws stepfunctions start-execution \

     --input '{"since_date": "2025-01-01", "run_analytics": false}'
   ```

3. Check CloudWatch logs for filter message:
   ```
   Filtered by since_date=2025-01-01: 1500 -> 42 receipts
   ```

Adds production-ready implementation guide for building Minimal APIs using CQRS pattern in .NET 6, covering architecture setup, authentication, and data access patterns.

## New Documentation

**`.github/instructions/minimal-api-cqrs-guide.md`** (1,602 lines)
- Architecture overview: Minimal APIs + CQRS separation of concerns
- Project scaffolding with .NET CLI and required packages (MediatR, Dapper, FluentValidation)
- Complete CQRS implementation with handlers:
  ```csharp
  public record CreateProductCommand(string Name, decimal Price, ...) : IRequest<CreateProductResult>;
  
  public class CreateProductCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateProductCommand, CreateProductResult>
  {
      public async Task<CreateProductResult> Handle(CreateProductCommand request, ...)
      {
          const string sql = @"INSERT INTO Products (...) VALUES (...)";
          var productId = await connection.ExecuteScalarAsync<int>(sql, request);
          return new CreateProductResult(productId, true, "Success");
      }
  }
  ```
- Program.cs configuration with MediatR pipeline and endpoint mappings
- SQL schema with indexes and Dapper factory pattern integration
- Dual auth strategies: JWT bearer tokens and Microsoft Entra ID
- Production features: error middleware, FluentValidation pipeline behavior, filtering/sorting/pagination, response caching, rate limiting

## Documentation Cross-linking

- `cqrs-pattern.md`: Added reference to detailed guide
- `SETUP.md`: Linked comprehensive implementation
- `README.md`: Added "Implementation Guides" section with all pattern documentation

## Example: Endpoint Mapping with MediatR

```csharp
app.MapPost("/api/products", async (CreateProductCommand command, IMediator mediator) =>
{
    var result = await mediator.Send(command);
    return result.Success 
        ? Results.Created($"/api/products/{result.ProductId}", result)
        : Results.BadRequest(result);
})
.RequireAuthorization()
.WithName("CreateProduct");
```

Query handler with advanced filtering:
```csharp
var sql = $@"
    SELECT * FROM Products
    WHERE {whereClause}
    ORDER BY {sortColumn} {sortDirection}
    OFFSET @Offset ROWS FETCH NEXT @PageSize ROWS ONLY";
```

Eliminates manual testing during PR development by enabling automated verification of backend health, frontend functionality, and UI changes through end-to-end tests with screenshot capture.

## Implementation

**E2E Test Suite** (`frontend/e2e/`)
- Authentication flows: login/logout, error handling
- Navigation: all major pages
- CRUD operations: Clients entity with form interactions
- Reusable test helpers for common operations

**Test Orchestration** (`run-tests.sh`)
- Starts backend API and frontend dev server
- Validates service health via endpoints
- Runs E2E tests with screenshot capture
- Captures logs (`backend.log`, `frontend.log`)
- Automatic cleanup on exit

**CI Integration** (`.github/workflows/dotnet.yml`)
- PostgreSQL service container for backend database
- Database migrations applied on startup (`Program.cs`)
- Health check endpoint (`/health`) for service readiness
- E2E tests run after backend tests complete
- Screenshots and HTML reports uploaded as artifacts (30-day retention)
- npm and Playwright browser caching (~2-3min savings on cache hits)
- Conditional execution: skips E2E tests and Docker build for draft PRs (~5-8min savings)

**Configuration**
- Playwright config for local/CI environments (90s test timeout, 60s action timeout)
- npm scripts: `test:e2e`, `test:e2e:ui`, `test:e2e:headed`, `test:e2e:debug`
- `.gitignore` updated to exclude test artifacts

## Usage

```bash
# Run complete test suite
./run-tests.sh

# Interactive debugging
cd frontend && npm run test:e2e:ui

# View results
ls frontend/screenshots/
npx playwright show-report
```

body:
### Motivation
- Replace HTTP polling with a single WebSocket-based price stream so Runtime, AI Observer and GUI consume the same live ticks without duplicated connections or blocking the UI. 
- Provide robust WS behavior including latency tracking, heartbeat monitoring and exponential reconnects to improve runtime resilience. 
- Ensure parallel consumers with no shared-state races by delivering ticks via per-subscriber queues and background workers. 

### Description
- Added a new `PriceFeedService` WebSocket module that connects to Binance trade stream, parses ticks into `PriceTick`, tracks exchange timestamps/latency, performs heartbeat checks, exposes CONNECTED/DEGRADED/LOST status and publishes ticks to subscribers via `_SubscriberWorker` queues (`src/services/price_feed_service.py`).
- Migrated `RuntimeEngine` to accept a shared `PriceFeedService`, subscribe/unsubscribe safely, consume `PriceTick` objects (exchange timestamp, latency), maintain timestamped price history, and compute micro-volatility/impulse metrics used for AI recommendations (`src/runtime/engine.py`).
- Updated `TradingRuntimeWindow` to create/subscribe to the shared `PriceFeedService`, forward ticks into Qt signals and display live price, latency and WS status, and to unsubscribe/stop the feed on close to avoid leaks (`src/gui/trading_runtime_window.py`).
- Removed the old HTTP-based runtime `PriceFeed` implementation and disabled HTTP fallback in `PriceService` so WS is the primary price source, preventing duplicate/competing flows (`src/runtime/price_feed.py` deleted, `src/services/price_service.py` updated).
- Implemented safe subscriber status callbacks (wrapped to match internal queue worker API) and non-blocking delivery so Runtime and GUI do not block each other.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed in this change; manual runtime validation was the intended next step and none was performed as part of this PR.

author: eigendude
body:
### Motivation
- Support magnetometer updates in the AHRS EKF core with the same style and injection path used by gyro/accel updates.  
- Provide a direction-only option for mag measurements (unit-vector updates are common for magnetometers).  
- Add simple covariance-matching/adaptive R support so the mag noise can be initialized from samples and adapted on-line.

### Description
- Add `oasis_control/oasis_control/localization/ahrs/ahrs_update_mag.py` implementing the magnetometer measurement model, Jacobians for attitude and world-field `m_w`, optional direction-only handling, Mahalanobis gating, and an `mag_alpha`-based covariance matching update.  
- Expose new config fields `mag_gate_d2_threshold: float` and `mag_use_direction_only: bool` in `AhrsConfig` and wire them into `ahrs_params.py` with defaults (`mag_gate_d2_threshold=9.0`, `mag_use_direction_only=True`).  
- Wire the mag update into `AhrsFilter`: `_apply_event()` now calls `update_mag(...)` for MAG events and stores a stateful `_mag_r_cov` that seeds/adapts the measurement covariance between updates.  
- Add unit tests `oasis_control/test/test_ahrs_update_mag.py` that verify acceptance of consistent measurements, rejection via Mahalanobis gating, and correct behavior for direction-only mode; update existing AHRS test config constructors to include the new config fields.

### Testing
- Ran the full test suite via `tox -q`.  
- All tests passed: `88 passed` (see tox output), including the new `test_ahrs_update_mag.py` cases.  
- Lint/type checks completed successfully during the tox run.

Editors need menu editing capability but must not access themes, widgets, or customizer.

## Implementation

**Capability management** (`lib/functions-capabilities.php`):
- Grant `edit_theme_options` to editor role via `after_switch_theme` and `admin_init` hooks
- Use `map_meta_cap` filter to restrict `edit_theme_options` to nav-menus.php and whitelisted menu AJAX actions only
- Block `switch_themes`, `edit_themes` for editors
- Hide non-menu appearance submenu items from editor UI

**Performance**:
- Static cache for user role checks (filter runs on every capability check)
- Extensible via `nm_editor_allowed_menu_actions` filter

**Security**:
- Whitelisted AJAX actions: `add-menu-item`, `delete-menu-item`, `update-menu-item`, etc.
- Input sanitization with `sanitize_text_field()` and `wp_unslash()`
- Admins retain full access

if ( $cap === 'edit_theme_options' ) {
  global $pagenow;
  if ( $pagenow === 'nav-menus.php' || $is_menu_ajax ) {

}
return array( 'do_not_allow' );

**Model Architecture Classes**
- `MultimodalFraudDetectionTransformer` - Three-stage architecture (tabular encoder, image encoder, cross-modal fusion)
- `FraudDetectionTransformer` - Tabular-only variant for backward compatibility

**Attention Mechanism Classes**
- `MultiHeadSelfAttention` - Standard scaled dot-product attention with multi-head parallelization
- `CrossModalAttention` - Bidirectional attention between tabular and image modalities
- `MaskedMultiHeadAttention` - Causal masking for autoregressive tasks

**Transformer Block Classes**
- `TransformerBlock` - Encoder block with self-attention + FFN + residual connections
- `CrossModalTransformerBlock` - Bidirectional cross-modal fusion with separate FFNs per modality
- `TransformerDecoderBlock` - Decoder with masked attention and encoder cross-attention

**Embedding and Layer Classes**
- `PatchEmbedding` - Vision Transformer patch extraction with position embeddings
- `FeedForward` - Position-wise FFN (d_model → dff → d_model)
- `ResidualConnection` - Add & Norm wrapper for sublayers

**Data Preprocessing Classes**
- `FraudDataPreprocessor` - Handles Online Payments Fraud Detection dataset format (encoding, scaling, reshaping)
- `QRCodePreprocessor` - Image loading, resizing to 224×224, normalization [0,1]
- `MultimodalDataPreprocessor` - Coordinates synchronized preprocessing across modalities

**Prediction and Inference Classes**
- `MultimodalFraudDetectionPredictor` - Production inference with automatic GPU config and batch processing
- `FraudDetectionPredictor` - Tabular-only inference for legacy systems

### Documentation Format

Each class includes:
- Purpose and architectural role
- Complete usage examples with configuration
- Mathematical formulations (attention mechanisms)
- Pipeline diagrams (ASCII flows)
- Design rationale and benefits
- Performance characteristics and use cases

### Example Documentation Structure

```python
from src.models.transformer import MultimodalFraudDetectionTransformer

config = {
    'd_model': 256,
    'num_heads': 8,
    'num_layers': 4,
    'cross_modal_layers': 2,
    'patch_size': 16,
    ...
}

model_builder = MultimodalFraudDetectionTransformer(config)
model = model_builder.build_model()
model = model_builder.compile_model(learning_rate=0.001)
```

Updated Table of Contents to reference new section 6.2.1.

author: mrsimpson
body:
## High level changes
• Created version-info.ts utility module with git-based version detection • Modified get-tool-info.ts to use dynamic version instead of hardcoded string • Replaced static '3.1.6-monorepo' with runtime version determination ## Motivation
MCP clients needed to identify which version of the responsible-vibe server they're running, but version information was hardcoded and outdated. This change enables clients to programmatically determine server version for compatibility checks and debugging. ## Details
The version-info.ts module implements a multi-source version detection strategy:
- Primary: Git describe command (git describe --tags --always --dirty) for development
- Secondary: package.json version as fallback
- Tertiary: Prepared BUILD_TIME_VERSION constant for future build-time injection
- Fallback: 'unknown' version with appropriate source indication Version information includes semantic version, git commit hash, dirty status, and source attribution. The getFormattedVersion() function provides human-readable output like '4.8.0+bbb06ba.dirty' that combines all relevant version components. Integration with get-tool-info.ts replaces the hardcoded version field, making the API response reflect actual running server version. This works in all environments: local development shows commit details, CI/CD uses git tags, and production deployments will show appropriate version information without requiring CI changes.

author: copilot
body:
AI learning metrics (dork success rates, extraction patterns) were tracked in SQLite but isolated from the CRM. This implements automatic sync of successful dorks to Django's SearchDork model, enabling continuous learning from real results.

### Model Changes (`SearchDork`)
- Added `leads_with_phone`, `total_search_results` for granular tracking
- Added JSONFields: `extraction_patterns`, `top_domains`, `phone_patterns` to store learned patterns
- Added `last_synced_at` timestamp and `update_from_learning_metrics()` method

### New `DorkSyncService`
- Bridges SQLite learning DB ↔ Django CRM
- Auto-creates SearchDork entries for successful AI-discovered dorks
- Configurable limits via class constants (`MAX_EXTRACTION_PATTERNS`, etc.)

### AI Learning Engine Integration
```python
# Now syncs to CRM automatically when leads have phone numbers
learning_engine.record_dork_result(
    dork="site:example.com Vertrieb",
    results=10,
    leads_found=5,
    leads_with_phone=3,
    sync_to_crm=True,  # default
    extraction_patterns=["div.phone"],
    top_domains=["example.com"],
)
```

### Management Command
```bash
python manage.py sync_dork_metrics --create-new --dry-run
```

### Migration
`0008_searchdork_ai_learning_fields.py` adds all new fields.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>
